articleTitle: A Collimator Study Towards BNCT-SPECT Systems for Dose Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We report the results of a study for the design of a collimator for a BNCT-SPECT system. The goal of the BNCT-SPECT system is to quantify and localize the dose released to a patient during a BNCT treatment, by detecting the 478 keV gamma rays emitted by the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>B(n,α)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>Li reactions. However, the extreme high intensity neutron flux of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> n/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/s and the mixed radiation field present in the irradiation room make this task very challenging. Therefore, the use of an appropriate collimator is required to optimize the Signal/Background ratio and perform tomographic imaging. We propose a detection system based on a 5 cm×5 cm×2 cm LaBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Ce+Sr) scintillator crystal, coupled to a matrix of 64 Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs). ANTS2 simulations have been used to design a pinhole lead collimator, optimizing both the spatial resolution (< 1 cm) and the geometric efficiency (>10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>). A final analytical study have been carried out to confirm the feasibility of our prototype to realize a full ring BNCT-SPECT system.

articleTitle: Results of Planar Pixel Sensors Qualification Campaign for the CMS Phase 2 Upgrade
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN will install a new Inner Tracker (IT) pixel detector for the High-Luminosity upgrade of LHC (HL-LHC). The maximum delivered integrated luminosity expected at the end of the HL-LHC running phase will be 4000fb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. At the innermost layer of the IT, a fluence corresponding to a non-ionizing energy loss (NIEL) of Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf> =3.5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> is expected. In this paper, the final design option chosen for planar silicon sensors of the IT will be reviewed. All the layers excluding the innermost of the barrel section of the IT will be equipped with planar n-in-p sensors with an active thickness of 150 μm and pixel size of 25 μm × 100 μm. The sensors used for this characterization campaign were coupled to a demonstrator chip (RD53A) and the modules were irradiated to different fluences up to Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf> =2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> and extensively tested in both CERN and DESY test beam facilities over the last three years. This campaign completed the first step of the vendor qualification and the results obtained are a reference for the next testing phase, based on the final CMS readout chip (CROC). An overview of the results obtained in terms of spatial resolution, hit efficiency, crosstalk, and noise studies is presented. For all the parameters investigated, the results were found to be within the requirements. This made it possible to qualify three vendors and promises excellent performances also for the pre-production phase that will start soon.

articleTitle: Spatial Optimization for Directional Detectors of γ-Rays Using Approximate Simulations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: A versatile optimization process is developed to improve γ-ray directional detection, using spatial arrangements of many detection units. The iterative process utilizes a novel approximate simulation to quickly estimate the detector’s response to low energy γ photons. Successful executions reveal superior structures for a notable deep-space γ-ray burst localization mission.

articleTitle: Commissioning Results and Operational Experience of the First Triple-GEM Station of the CMS Muon System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: As part of CMS upgrade strategy of the muon system towards HL-LHC, a new station of triple-GEM detectors (GE1/1) has been installed in both endcaps of the CMS detector. This additional muon station will allow dealing with the high luminosity conditions imposed by HL-LHC, improving the trigger capabilities in the forward region. The station was installed in 2020 and consists of 72 ten-degree super-chambers, each made up of two layers of triple-GEM detectors. GE1/1 provides the CMS muon system with two additional muon hit measurements which will improve muon tracking and triggering performance while allow to keep the muon trigger rate under control without the need to increase the threshold on the muon transverse momentum. This report will describe the status of the commissioning phase of the detector. It will additionally present preliminary results from the first runs with the LHC beams. Attention will be given to issues encountered during CMS magnet commissioning which induced trips and short-circuits in the GEM detectors. Therefore, the results of a dedicated test with magnetic field are shown in light of the observed behavior in CMS.

articleTitle: Investigation of Network Architecture for Multimodal Head-and-Neck Tumor Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Inspired by the recent success of transformers for Natural Language Processing and vision transformer for Computer Vision, many researchers in the medical imaging community have flocked to transformer-based networks for various main stream medical tasks such as classification [1] - [3] segmentation [4] - [6] and registration [7], [8]. In this study, we analyze, two recently published transformer-based network architectures for the task of multimodal head-and-tumor segmentation and compare their performance to the de facto standard 3D segmentation network – the nnU-Net. Our results showed that modelling long-range dependencies may be helpful in cases where large structures are present and/or large field of view is needed. However, for small structures such as head-and-neck tumor, the convolution-based U-Net architecture seemed to perform well, especially when training dataset is small and computational resource is limited.

articleTitle: Towards an On-Chip Analog Neural Network for Position Sensitivity in Anger Cameras
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We present the study of an analog hardware accelerator targeting the implementation of on-chip Neural Network (NN) inference for ADC-less and FPGA-less position sensitivity in Anger Cameras. We report high-level simulations based on MATLAB to emulate the operation of a 64-32-32-2 NN implemented in a CMOS process, exploring two reference studies: a PET detector and a SPECT detector, achieving a spatial resolution of 1.38 mm and 0.84 mm FWHM, respectively. The network parameters (weights, biases, and activation function) are then exploited in the design of a programmable, switched capacitor (SC)-based matrix for executing in charge domain the multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations needed for an inference step.

articleTitle: MRI Radiomic Features Harmonization: A Multi-Center Phantom Study
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In cancer imaging, radiomic features are a vital tool for diagnosing, quantifying intratumor heterogeneity, and predicting response to therapy and prognosis. However, the lack of a robust evaluation makes applying them across multi-center studies and larger patient populations complex. The main goal of this study is to use an MRI phantom to examine the reproducibility of MRI radiomic features that represent feature variability with ComBat harmonization in a multi-center examination with various acquisition settings and image pre-processing steps. An MRI phantom was used to acquire images using four scanners. Manual segmentation was used for 19 phantom compartments. Wavelet, bin discretization, and Laplacian of Gaussian were employed to pre-process each image. Ninety-two radiomic features were extracted. ComBat harmonization was applied to all feature sets. The Kruskal-(KW) Wallis’s and the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) tests were utilized to indicate radiomic features’ variability. The number of non-significant p-values ranged from 29-74 and 0-5 features after and before harmonization over different image pre-processing. The results showed that the radiomic features are influenced most by various scanners. The impact of ComBat harmonization on the reproducibility of MRI radiomic features is considerable.

articleTitle: Novel Circuit Design for a 3D Position Sensitive Scintillation TOF-PET Detector that Achieves ~100 ps CTR
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We have built a scalable mixed-signal readout circuit for a 3D position sensitive PET detector that achieves ~100 ps FWHM CTR. For this work we used individual 3×3×3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and 3×3×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> LGSO crystals, as well as 2×4 arrays of 3×3×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> crystals side-coupled to arrays of 3.16×3.16 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> SiPMs. The preliminary results verify that the CPLD is able to resolve 3D interaction positions along the array with < 3 mm positioning resolution along the length of each 10 mm long crystal element. We also present the readout strategy to compensate the CPLD digital noise that otherwise reduces the sensitivity and CTR performance. With this novel strategy we achieved nearly %100 sensitivity recovery as well as ~11 ps improved CTR.

articleTitle: Physics, Transport Schemes and Empirical Algorithms in the Simulation of Electron Energy Deposition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Accurate simulation of the energy deposited by electrons in matter is an essential requirement of Monte Carlo particle transport codes. It involves multiple components present in these codes: physics models and parameters, the transport schemes adopted to deal with electron interactions, and empirical algorithms and parameters. In this conference paper we report new results of recent validation tests, which exploit high precision experimental measurements and an extensive set of simulation test cases to identify the contribution of different Geant4 components to the accuracy of the simulation of this observable. The validation tests concerns the series of Geant4 version 10 releases and the Geant4 11.0 version.

articleTitle: Timing Calibration with Depth of Interaction for the NeuroEXPLORER Brain PET
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The NeuroEXPLORER (NX) is a next generation SiPM based dedicated brain PET scanner. It offers ultra-high sensitivity, spatial resolution, and an extended axial field of view. To provide previously unachievable imaging performance, NX uses novel U-shaped LYSO crystals with reduced sizes to provide depth of interaction (DOI) and time of flight (TOF) measurements. Timing calibration is critical to achieve the best possible timing resolution. In this work, we investigate timing calibration with DOI for the NX. We develop an iterative algorithm to accurately estimate time offsets on a per crystal and DOI basis using a line source. We first estimate the source position using, e.g., a non-TOF reconstruction. The difference time error for each event is computed by comparing the measured time and true time obtained based on the source position, which in turn is used to generate error histograms for each DOI of each crystal. The mean is estimated from a Gaussian fitting, which is used as a candidate for updating time offsets using an iterative algorithm. To further reduce data acquisition time, we introduce a separable time offset model (STOM), the time offsets are mainly contributed by crystal and DOI independently. The STOM allows timing calibration incorporating DOI information while reducing unknowns comparable to those in a non-DOI timing calibration. The overall mean timing resolution in FWHM is 271.3±13.9ps. The difference between STOM time offsets and full estimated time offsets is quite small; the standard error is about 1 TOF bin of 12.21ps. In summary, we develop effective timing calibration with DOI using a line source for the NX.

articleTitle: Electronic Readout for a 100 ps CTR PET Detector with 24:1 Multiplexing Ratio of Timing Channels
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We have designed a novel electronic readout with 24:1 multiplexing ratio of the timing channels that achieves 100 ps coincidence time resolution. The detector layer units comprise 2×4 arrays of 3×3×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> "LGSO" crystals side-coupled to 6×4 arrays of 3×3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> SiPMs. To achieve low power dissipation and scalability of this readout design, its effective area is implemented in only 13.3 mm using compact and power efficient electronic components. The measured CTR of the 24:1 multiplexed timing channels (or 8:1 LVDS signals) was 107.0 ± 3.6 ps FWHM using a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sup>Na point-source and a very low timing jitter FPGA-based TDC.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of Material Decomposition in Dual-Energy Radiography for Bone Removal
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Dual-energy X-ray imaging provides additional image information, which can be exploited to conduct material decomposition. Using a projection-domain material decomposition approach is expected to be superior to a weighted logarithmic subtraction. The path length of bone and water per-pixel in an image can be calculated by interpolation in precalculated look-up tables of low- and high-energy attenuation values. Precalculation of the attenuation values makes an accurate spectrum estimation necessary. This can be achieved by adjusting the tube voltage and inherent aluminum (Al) filtration of an analytical X-ray spectrum model. When applied to ray-tracing simulation data, projection-domain decomposition outperforms a weighted logarithmic subtraction. When applied to measurement data without any scatter correction applied, the combination of spectrum estimation and look-up table-based decomposition provides images that are qualitatively comparable to them obtained by weighted logarithmic subtraction. Images obtained by look-up table-based decomposition show artefacts that are most likely due to the presence of scatter which we plan to tackle in the future.

articleTitle: A Compact Front-End Circuit for a Monolithic Sensor in a 65 nm CMOS Imaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This work presents the design of a front-end circuit optimized for a monolithic active pixel sensor with a small, low-capacitance collection electrode. This work was carried out in the framework of the CERN-EP R&D on monolithic sensors and the ALICE ITS3 upgrade in a first exploration of the TowerJazz Panasonic Semiconductor (TPSCo) 65 nm imaging technology. The circuit was integrated into a 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm proof-of-principle prototype, the Digital Pixel Test Structure or DPTS, featuring a sensitive area of 32 × 32 pixels with a 15 μm pitch. The front-end occupies an area of ~ 42 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and, together with the digital readout, allowed this small pitch. The sensor was optimized to reduce charge sharing and concentrate charge on the seed pixel as much as possible to increase operating margin. This very first prototype proved fully efficient in test beam, validating not only the front-end but also the sensor and the digital readout circuitry. First measurement results on the front-end will also be shown.

articleTitle: ePixHR10k 2M – A 2M Pixel X-ray Detector at 5,000 Frame Per Second for LCLS-II
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The tender X-ray beamline at LCLS-II, a Free Electron Laser (FEL) X-ray light source, is set to start operations at SLAC National laboratory in 2023 exploring x-ray energies from 2 to 4 keV. The beamline requires a camera system with 2 Mega pixels capable of sustaining readout rates higher than 5,000 frames per second compatible with the matrix of the ePixHR10k sensor/ASIC modules. The detector also needs to have a segmented focal plane with an adjustable gap between top and bottom planes that are capable of remote positioning, operate in vacuum and have high quantum efficiency. We present in this paper a detector called ePixHR10k 2M that can fulfil these requirements. The camera design is based on a shingled tile arrangement to minimize gaps among rows of detector modules.

articleTitle: Fully Automated Multi-Organ Segmentation in CT Images via Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Organ segmentation is essential in medical imaging applications in radiation therapy, diagnostic organ dosimetry, and computational quantitative calculations such as radiomics studies and theranostic. Manual segmentation of clinical data is labor-intensive and time-consuming, besides the inter-observer differences remain a problem. In this study, we tried to do the automatic segmentation of multiple organs from CT images. We collected CT images and organ segmentations for the Liver (157 cases), Pancreas (390 cases), Kidneys (310 cases), Spleen (70 cases), Bladder (112 cases), Aorta (30 cases), and Gallbladder (295 cases). After pre-processing, including resizing and rescaling, data were split into train/validation (80%) and test (20%) groups. A residual deep neural network was trained to segment images. The performance was evaluated by the Dice and Jaccard Coefficient of the output compared with the ground truth for each organ. The average dice values were 0.96±0.02, 0.78±0.2, 0.90±0.19, 0.94 ±0.08, 0.85±0.16, 0.85±0.06, and 0.79±0.2 for the Liver, Pancreas, Kidney, Spleen, Bladder, Aorta, and Gallbladder, respectively. Also, the Jaccard values were 0.92 ± 0.02, 0.65 ± 0.20, 0.84 ± 0.19, 0.90 ± 0.08, 0.77 ± 0.18, 0.75 ± 0.08, 0.69 ± 0.21 for the mentioned organs, respectively. The best dice were for the liver, followed by the spleen, while the weakest performance was shown in pancreas and gall bladder segmentation. The performance of our network was comparable with the recent studies in this field, while we included the data from multiple sources in the test set. This fully automatic segmentation pipeline can decrease the treatment planning time in radiation therapy and make the dosimetry in theranostic feasible. Also, it can be helpful to generate computational phantoms by anchor organ segmentation.

articleTitle: SITH: a 16-channel ASIC for SiPMs Readout in Hadrontherapy Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In hadrontherapy treatments, charged particles deposit a high and localized dose in the tumor volume. Detection of secondary radiations like Prompt Gammas (PG) can be used to monitor the dose profile falloff position, increasing the precision of this technique. In this work we present the design of SITH: an ASIC developed for the readout of Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) coupled with scintillators used in this application. PG characteristics set specific requirements for the front-end electronics such as the capability to process up to 5nC input charge (energy up to 8MeV), timing resolution better than 1ns (e.g. for scattering correction), multiple triggering logic and potential for neutron/photon discrimination. We report an overview of the principal electronic stages and simulation results.

articleTitle: A Pilot Study of Attenuation Correction for Static and Dynamic 13N-Ammonia Cardiac PET Using a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Attenuation correction (AC) of myocardial perfusion PET remains challenging in routine clinical practice due to the potential misalignment of PET and CT data, which results in image artifacts and inaccurate quantitative parameters in PET/CT. In this work, a 3D conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) was used to directly generate attenuation-corrected PET (PET-AC) images from non-attenuation-corrected PET (PET-NAC) images. This work included 60 patients who underwent rest <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>N-ammonia PET/CT examinations. For each patient, one static PET and twenty-one dynamic PET frames were acquired with both AC and NAC. The network was firstly trained by 3D paired static <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>N-ammonia PET-NAC and CT-based AC PET (PET-CTAC) images in an end-to-end fashion (PET-DLAC). Then the pre-trained network was fine-tuned (FT) by 3D paired dynamic PET-NAC and PET-CTAC frames (PET-DLAC-FT). Five-fold cross-validation was adopted to train and test the network. Qualitative and quantitative analyses were performed by voxel-wise analysis on the standard intake values (SUV), e.g., RMSE, PSNR, SSIM, and joint histogram analysis versus the PET-CTAC images as reference. Furthermore, quantitative kinetic parameters and time activity curves of the dynamic PET were performed to evaluate the PET-DLAC-FT method. Qualitative and quantitative results show the proposed PET-DLAC and PET-DLAC-FT methods reduce attenuation artifacts significantly and achieve comparable performances with clinical CTAC. Transfer learning-based AC is feasible for dynamic cardiac PET.

articleTitle: Deep Image Prior PET Reconstruction using a SIRF-Based Objective
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Widespread adoption of deep learning in medical imaging has been hampered, in part, due to a lack of integration with clinically applicable software. In this work, we establish a direct connection between an established PET reconstruction suite, SIRF, and PyTorch. This allows for advanced reconstruction methodologies to be deployed on clinical data with an unsupervised deep learning approach: the Deep Image Prior. Results show consistent quality metrics for DIP in comparison to OSMAP.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Feature Learning Ability of UNet from Different Transforms of List-mode Data in TOF PET
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Deep learning technique has been combined with traditional analytical image reconstruction algorithms recently for fast reconstruction of denoised images in TOF PET. Researchers used different transforms of list-mode data as the input to the deep learning model in these works. However, different inputs have not been investigated under the same circumstance. In this work, we trained deep models with completely the same network architecture but with different forms of input images, such as the histo-images and the back-projection images. The models were trained using simulated brain phantoms and then tested with both simulated data and clinical data. The reconstructed images and quantitative comparison suggested that deep learning models learned the best features from the back-projected image of pre-corrected list-mode data acquired by TOF PET.

articleTitle: Mice PET/CT Dataset Augmentation Using a 3D-Progressive Growing GAN
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this study, we applied GANs for synthetic 3D mice generation, to be used in PET/CT preclinical deep learning (DL) based research. The lack of available datasets makes it difficult for researchers to apply DL to solve tasks that involve small-animal data, such as emission-based attenuation correction in small-animals’ PET/MR. We applied a 3D-Progressive Growing GAN (3D-PGAN) to generate synthetic CT scans of mice. The 3D-PGAN generated a 64 x 64 x 160 CT scan of a mouse in approximately 0.10 seconds with a Fréchet inception distance (FID), which measures the similarity between two datasets of images, of 103.1 on the coronal plane. For reference, a FID of 0 indicates perfect similarity, and a score of 103.1 is comparable to related works’ results. The generated CT scans resembled real CT scans; however, the generated images were often missing finer structures like a mouse’s ribcage.

articleTitle: Density Dedicated Deep Learning Model for Mammogram Malignancy Classification
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: A body of literature has reported the promising performance of deep learning models when applied to mammograms for different clinical tasks. However, a major pitfall of deep learning models is when they are applied to mammograms bearing high-density breasts since the overlapping high-dense tissue can cover the lesion and make diagnosing and interpreting it difficult. Thus, analysis of dedicated models trained for low- and high-dense breasts can be of great importance. In this study, we aimed to develop low- and high-density dedicated deep-learning models for classifying breast masses on mammograms into benign and malignant cases. Curated Breast Imaging Subset of the Digital Database for Screening Mammography (CBIS-DDSM) dataset, including mammograms, cropped to masses, and the pathologic diagnoses, were adopted for this study. For dedicated models, the dataset was split into low-(BI-RADS density1 and 2) and high-dense (BI-RADS density3 and 4) groups. Contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) was applied to enhance the contrast of the images, and then all images were resized to 255 × 255 matrix size and normalized. A modified DenseNet-201 deep neural network was trained with the learning rate starting at 0.0001 and decreased in a piecewise manner every epoch with the RMSProp optimizer. Fifteen percent of training data was excluded for validation, and training was continued for 100 epochs. Data augmentation, including rotation, flipping, and scaling, was implemented on the training dataset to prevent overfitting. The trained model was evaluated using the test set. Accuracy (ACC), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity (SEN), and specificity (SPE) for the general model were 0.720, 0.771, 0.732, 0.701, for the Low-density model were 0.788, 0.818, 0.824, and 0.742, and for High-density model was 0.712, 0.621, 0.962, and 0.180, respectively. Our study highlights the importance of developing dedicated models tailored to the nature of high-density breasts to improve overall accuracy. We also suggest performing specific preprocessing for high-density breasts, such as region-wise contrast enhancement for the regions with high-intensity values (with a gamma filter, etc.).

articleTitle: Prior Simulation Test of a Total Body PET Scanner with Multiple Configurations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Total Body PET systems improve their capabilities by reaching more sensitivity than conventional PET scanners. Through Monte Carlo simulations, this work compares two different PET designs with similar dimensions (20 cm axial coverage) but different technologies (LYSO and BGO). This is a pilot study, new simulations extending the axial FOV to about 70 cm are undergoing.The first technology is based on LYSO slabs (25 × 3 × 20 mm, monolithic × pixel × height) that can combine good DOI information and a Detector Time Resolution (DTR) below 250 ps. The second one is based on thicker BGO pixelated crystals (3 × 3 × 30 mm), increasing the sensitivity but reducing the system cost. NEMA NU 2018 sensitivity and spatial resolution protocols were implemented for both configurations. The Jaszczack phantom has also been simulated to evaluate the Contrast to Noise Ratio (CNR). Besides the BGO system resulted on a superior sensitivity, the spatial resolution in the LYSO scanner is better than 3 mm in all the FOV and provides a superior performance in terms of image quality.

articleTitle: Reliability of 3D Pixelated CdZnTe System in the Quantitative Assay of Radioactive Waste: a Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Several tests have been performed with an H420 pixelated CdZnTe imaging spectrometer to evaluate its capability to provide reliable imaging and quantification results. Waste barrels prepared by National Physical Laboratory (NPL) for the Nuclear Industry Proficiency Test Exercise held in 2019 and 2021 were measured, detecting clear <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">241</sup>Am, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">137</sup>Cs, and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co photopeaks in collected gamma-ray spectra, while Compton and coded aperture imaging were used to localize sources and reconstruct their 2D/3D spatial distributions. Point-kernel-based activity quantification techniques were used to estimate isotope-specific activities, with results close to those obtained by High Purity Germanium detectors and to true NPL declarations. Furthermore, in order to test the reliability of the quantification method for a large span of energies/distances/materials, a hot <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">226</sup>Ra source was measured in multiple geometries, obtaining consistent data, although difficulties in measuring peak areas on large, non-linear continua were observed. The results presented in this work suggests that high-resolution 3D pixelated CdZnTe detectors can be used for typical waste quantification problems and can reliably assay complex geometries thanks to flexibility of the quantification algorithm. Moreover, the spatial information on the radionuclides’ distribution from gamma-ray imaging can be used as input for a heterogeneous radioactivity model to minimize systematic uncertainties.

articleTitle: Emission-Based Attenuation Correction for Small Animal PET/MR Using Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this work, we applied conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) for emission-based attenuation correction (AC) in small animals and evaluated the performance of our solution on the generated attenuation map and the AC reconstructed images. The non-attenuated and scatter corrected reconstructed image was fed into the cGAN that was trained to generate the corresponding attenuation map. This generated attenuation map was then converted into a pCT and fed into the image reconstruction software one more time to correct the generated PET image for photon attenuation. Using our method, we can generate high quality PET images without performing a CT scan, PSNR of 43.49dB and SSIM of 0.998 compared to the CT-based AC PET.

articleTitle: Projection Restoration from Filtered-Backprojection Images of Sparse-View CT
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Projection data has been considered essential to improve the image quality of filtered-backprojection (FBP) results in computed tomography (CT), especially when the projection is corrupted. In recent years, the emerging deep learning (DL)-based algorithms made it possible to improve the FBP image quality without any projection data by training deep neural networks for image-to-image mapping. However, networks that incorporate both projection and image data still generally show better performance compared to image-only networks. Despites of the advantages, projection data are usually hard to acquire for most researchers and costly to store and process. In this work, we propose a novel method to restore the projection data from the FBP images. The method iteratively optimizes the projection such that its FBP reconstruction matches the original, corrupted FBP image. Furthermore, the restored projection can be used to improve the DL-FBP images using iterative reconstruction (IR). Sparse-view CT with parallel beam was simulated from both Forbild head phantom a Mayo Low-dose Challenge dataset to validate the algorithm. Results showed that the proposed method reduced the projection estimation error by 90% compared to forward projection from the sparse-view FBP and 50% compared to that from the DL results. Post-DL IR using the restored projection also improved the image textures and reduced the residual streaking artifacts.

articleTitle: Characteristics of an Endcap Detector that Improves Geometric Efficiency for Imaging Two or More Tracers in the Same Imaging Session
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) provides molecular information in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases ranging from cancer to neurological disorders through the imaging of biological tracers injected before imaging. Current PET systems are unable to image more than one tracer simultaneously because a conventional PET system only accepts events falling within an energy window centered on the 511 keV annihilation photopeak. Previous studies have proposed to differentiate multiple PET tracers in the same imaging session by employing positron emitters that also emit prompt high-energy gamma photons in cascade with the positron. The detection of this higher energy gamma photon in coincidence with the annihilation photon pair forms a 3-photon coincidence that can be attributed to a specific tracer. But the sensitivity of a conventional PET ring to 3-photon coincidences is low, yielding low quality reconstructed images. This paper outlines simulation studies conducted using an additional endcap detector which covers the open end of an existing 30 cm diameter, 16 cm length PET ring system for brain imaging. The simulation studies showed the addition of a 2 cm thick LSO endcap detector could provide up to a 3.24x increase in sensitivity to 3-photon coincidences over using no endcap and increasing the thickness of the endcap detector to 4 cm of LSO could further increase the system sensitivity by 50%.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of a Dynamic Dual-head Breast PET Scanner Based on LSO and CZT Detector Modules: a Simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Breast PET scanners can be used for early diagnosis of breast cancer and decline the number of women who "call back" for extra evaluations/tests in response to breast cancer. Our designed scanner is equipped with two planar detectors the size of 4 × 12 × 15 cm and 180 crystal segments with dimensions of 4 × 4 × 0.5 cm their separation distance can mechanically adjust between 4 cm to 8 cm. Two types of detector materials include Lutetium Oxyorthoscilicate LSO(Ce) scintillator and Cadmium Zinc Telluride (CZT) were used separately to evaluate their performance. For scanning first, the patient lay in a prone state on a dedicated bed with two adjustable holes on it where both patient's breasts were located in the holes. As the scanner is dual head, doing transformation between the breasts is easy and can perform through a robotic arm that moves the PET detector's heads from the first to the second breast. Two different scanning approaches were performed in this study, first, the gantry was kept fixed and a partial scan was achieved (Static-scan) and second the detectors start to rotate 90 degrees around the patient’s breast to collect fully tomographic datasets (Dynamic-scan).To assess our designed scanner the spatial resolution, sensitivity, and noise equivalent count ratio (NECR) are estimated based on the NEMA NU-4-2008 standard.The static scan with LSO and CZT lead to a sensitivity of 50.8% and 31.1% and a spatial resolution of 6.4 mm and 1.6 mm, respectively. While for the dynamic-scan, the sensitivity increased to 71.2% and 47.3%, and spatial resolution enhanced to 2.7 mm and 1.1 mm, for LSO and CZT respectively. The NECR for LSO has the highest count equivalent rate of 494 Kcts / sec while for the CZT detector is 200 kcts / sec. The CZT-based scanner shows higher spatial resolution while the LSO-based scanner provides higher sensitivity.

articleTitle: Histoimage-based Image Segmentation and Application in Organ Motion Detection in TOF PET
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In PET/CT, segmentation of anatomical structures is often performed on the CT. However, this practice assumes a PET-matched CT image is available, which can be violated due to patient movement between CT and PET acquisitions. This limitation may be addressed by segmenting organs based on the PET image itself, e.g., non-attenuation corrected (NAC) PET. With the improvement in TOF resolution of a PET scanner, e.g., uMI Panorama with 196-ps TOF, the anatomical structure in the histoimage, which is generated by back-projecting the TOF bin center of each event, can be used for image domain AI-based application. Unlike reconstructed PET, histoimage is very fast to compute and no image reconstruction is needed. In this work, we propose to perform AI-based organ segmentation based on the histoimage. Whole-body <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F-FDG PET/CT data (N = 140) were acquired on the United Imaging uMI Panorama PET/CT scanner. Segmentation based on the NAC PET is performed as comparison. Using training labels generated by a CT-based AI segmentation software, five individual neural networks were trained to segment heart, liver, left kidney, right kidney and spleen, respectively. Dice coefficients of the histoimage based segmentation were found 85.7 ± 7.2%, 85.7 ± 2.8%, 83.1 ± 6.7%, 78.8 ± 17.4% and 74.3 ± 8.8% for the five organs. For NAC PET, the statistics were 86.3 ± 6.0%, 86.8 ± 3.1%, 83.3 ± 6.6%, 82.3 ± 14.1% and 74.4 ± 8.7%. No statistical difference was found between the histoimage-based and NAC PET-based organ segmentation except for the right kidney. Finally, the segmented ROIs based on histoimage are applied to organ-specific data-driven respiratory motion tracking.

articleTitle: The Impact of Additional Sampling on Hot-Spot Contrast for DE-SPECT
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: DE-SPECT is a CZT-based system for assessing Peripheral Arterial Disease [1], [2]. Each CZT module is 4 cm x 4 cm x 1 cm. They are configured in a half-populated 4 x 4 array per panel – with 6 panels in the scanner – such that every other slot is populated. This configuration reduces cost, but also provides the opportunity to have two different collimator configurations, with one in front of the detectors at a time. An axial actuator switches between the two modes. Herein, the tradeoffs between sampling and sensitivity when utilizing that actuator for additional sampling positions are considered by using contrast to noise as the metric for evaluation. A metric of complete sampling was evaluated as a function of axial shift between acquisitions. In addition, a hot-spot phantom with hot spots configured at 27 positions on a 3x3x3 grid with 4 cm pitch was used to evaluate contrast. Three phantoms were considered: 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0 cm hot spots. Ensembles of 25 noise instances for shifts of 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 cm were considered. Three noise levels were considered: 640k, 2560k, and 10240k total count equivalents, where a count equivalent is a count in the nominal position, but considered the reduced efficiency for shifted projections; thus, equivalent duration was used. The optimal sampling occurs at 1.5 cm displacement. Optimal contrast occurred at 0.5 cm axial shift, for the shifts considered, for the 0.6 cm and 0.8 cm spheres. The advantage was more ambiguous for 1.0 cm spheres. Sensitivity drops off quickly with axial shift, limiting the advantage of additional sampling. The optimal tradeoff occurs between 0.0 cm and 1.0 cm. This study considered steps of 0.5 cm so far. In conclusion, hot-spot contrast can be improved by the addition of additional sampling provided by small axial shifts from the nominal detector position.

articleTitle: Low-Dose Tau PET Imaging Based on Swin Restormer with Diagonally Scaled Self-Attention
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Though successful and efficient in local feature extraction, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) cannot capture long-range dependencies well due to its limited receptive field. Transformer-based network structures can exploit the long-range information through a self-attention mechanism and have recently demonstrated better performance than CNN in various computer vision tasks. However, self-attention is hard to be directly applied to 3D images due to the computational cost. In this work, we proposed a novel transformer architecture, Swin Restormer, which integrates two efficient transformers, namely Swin Transformer and Restormer, to improve low-dose tau PET image quality. The proposed Swin Restormer can efficiently perform self-attention in both spatial and channel dimensions. A diagonally scaled self-attention mechanism was also proposed to further improve the attention map calculation. Quantitative evaluations based on clinical 18F-MK-6240 tau imaging datasets show that the proposed transformer architecture can achieve better denoising performance than the UNet structure.

articleTitle: Development of Position-Sensitive Capacitive Frisch-Grid CsPbBr3 Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Two CsPbBr3 Position-Sensitive Capacitive Frisch Grid (PS-CFG) detectors were fabricated and characterized. The devices’ sizes in planar configuration were 3×3×6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (nominal size). <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">137</sup>Cs spectra were collected from two detectors for the cathodes signal with no 3-D correction and with 3-D correction from one of the detectors. The synthesis and the crystal growth of the CsPbBr3 materials are presented, the detector fabrication process is described, and the resulting energy spectra are discussed. The use of the 3-D position sensing technique provides information on the crystal uniformity. This technique was applied and the spatial variation in the histograms of the cathode amplitude versus the anode-to-cathode ratio are presented and discussed. A 2.8% FWHM energy resolution at 662 keV was achieved after 3-D correction from the 3×3×6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> PS-CFG CsPbBr3 detector.

articleTitle: Novel High-Resolution Fully FPGA-based Detection Setup for High-Transfer Rate Time-Resolved Experiments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: With the advancement of new X-ray sources, such as synchrotron radiation facilities and Free Electron Lasers (FELs), which can generate high-flux and ultrashort X-ray pulses, time-resolved techniques have become general and powerful tools for exploring structural dynamics of matter. Thus, a new generation of acquisition system is needed, where the ability to temporally solve each measurement with great precision and versatility is required. Among the instruments most involved in this direction there are undoubtedly the particle detectors, which can no longer limit themselves to providing images but must be able to associate temporal information to each event received, in addition to the spatial one. With this in mind, Cross Delay-Lines (CDLs) detectors are among the most suitable and promising solutions allowing both spatial and temporal data to be acquired simultaneously. Typical architectures underlying the acquisition electronics of these detectors rely on an Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) followed by a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) for data processing. The lack of reconfigurability and the inadequacy of adapting to different applications given by the ASIC, has brought us to study a new solution. Our multi-year work proposes a fully FPGA-based architecture with the purpose of obtaining excellent time resolution and fast parallel computing while maintaining the full flexibility only an FPGA can achieve. The acquisition chain is comprised of two FPGA boards, one hosting a custom-made TDC while the other the necessary image reconstruction algorithm. Over the years we managed to design an 8-channel TDC with a precision of 12 ps r.m.s, 5 ns dead-time, and 4 ps of non-linearity reaching a spatial resolution of 30/40 μm FWHM on the CDL. Improvements to the connection between the TDC and the image processing board are been implemented allowing a transfer rate of tens Gb/s, which means hundreds of Mmeasures/s.

articleTitle: Prompt-gamma Energy Spectrum-based Simultaneous Dual-isotope PET Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Simultaneous dual-isotope PET imaging has great potential in clinical applications. The main challenge of dual-isotope PET imaging is that the coincidences from different nuclides cannot be distinguished by energy. According to the physical property of non-pure positron-emitting isotopes that an extra gamma photon is produced almost simultaneously with positron annihilation, the separation of the pure isotopes and the non-pure isotopes can be achieved based on the triple coincidence technique. However, not only do non-pure isotopes produce triple coincidences, but pure isotopes also generate random triple coincidences, which eventually lead to residues of the pure isotopes in the non-pure isotopes. In this study, a triple-coincidence correction strategy based on the prompt-gamma energy spectrum is proposed. First, the mixed energy spectrum of all the prompt photons in the triple coincidences is obtained. Then a Gaussian function is used to fit the energy spectrum of the ‘pseudo' prompt photons from the pure isotope, and thus the spectrum of the non-pure isotope is obtained from the mixed spectrum. According to both of the energy spectra, the number of triple coincidences generated by the non-pure isotope on each line of response is obtained by the moment estimation method. The phantom experiments of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">124</sup>I show that the proposed method improves the accuracy of reconstructed images qualitatively and quantitatively, compared with other triple-coincidence methods.

articleTitle: Passive CMOS Strip Detectors for High Energy Particle Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Current trackers and high energy particle experiments are populated with silicon detectors, which provide fast precise signal, can cover large areas and are available in silicon foundries. The utilization of a CMOS silicon foundry for fabricating large area silicon detectors is possible but the sensors should be stitched, connecting several reticles to form a strip, or a large area pixel. These detectors can be used for high energy particle detection as well as large area detectors for medical application. This project shows results of the first production of silicon strip detectors produced in a CMOS foundry with 150 nm technology using stitching of 1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> reticles. The wafer consist of high resistivity 150 μm thick float zone silicon. The strip detectors are fabricated in two sizes, 2.1 cm long and 4.1 cm long. Here the characterization, simulation and performance of those strip detectors under different applications will be shown, without and with irradiation of the silicon. We will demonstrate that stitching strips do not show any negative effect on their performance.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Analytical Methods Using Ion Beam Induced Luminescence
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Ion beam induced luminescence (IBIL) analysis has been employed as one means of accurately understanding the extraction behavior of wet separation methods, which are expected to achieve advanced separation performance as MA separation technology. IBIL analysis is a material analysis method that uses an ion beam to excite the outer shell electrons of an analyte and detects and analyzes the electromagnetic waves (Ion beam induced luminescence) of a few eV generated during the relaxation process. Since this measurement method focuses on the emission by outer-shell electrons, unlike PIXE or RBS analysis, it can provide information on bonding, but the value and methods of its use are still unclear. Therefore, the chemical composition of natural mineral pigments made from crushed natural ores was clarified by combining the ore luminescence database with IBIL and PIXE analyses, demonstrating the usefulness of these analytical methods.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation of Redundant Configuration in Xilinx FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Field programmable gate arrays play a key role in particle physics experiments for real-time data transfer and processing. The usage of such devices in the radiation environments of detectors at colliders or at fixed-target experiments requires to cope with radiation effects. Radiation-induced single event upsets in the device configuration are the dominant issue for static random access memory based field programmable gate arrays. Solutions based on configuration redundancy have been proposed for hardening the configuration memory of commercial off-the-shelf static-random-access-memory-based field programmable gate arrays. In these, the configuration is majority voted by the firmware to correct radiation-induced configuration upsets. In this work, we introduce an automatic methodology to generate a redundant configuration for static-random-access-memory-based field programmable gate arrays. The methodology is based on copying the configuration fragments to be protected to unused ones, measuring the impact of the copy on the power consumption of the field programmable gate array and on the functionality of the firmware. We implemented a hardware setup and a software tool to realize and test this idea. The method is completely agnostic with respect to the device, the only requirement being the possibility to write and read back the configuration. This is supported by most of the modern devices.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Beta-Decay Radioactive Nuclides with Energy Spectra and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This study applied machine learning using a neural network to analyze the nuclides from a beta-ray energy spectrum. Nuclides emitting gamma and alpha-rays are identified from the peak energy of their energy spectra. The shape of a typical beta-ray spectrum is continuous and has no apparent features such as the peak structure. This feature makes it difficult to identify nuclides from their energy spectra in the field. To overcome the challenge, we applied machine learning to beta-ray energy spectra. Five nuclides, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">90</sup>Sr, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">137</sup>Cs, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">204</sup>Tl, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">147</sup>Pm, and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co, were used for analysis to validate the method. A training dataset was created by Geant4 simulation. Beta-ray energy spectra were acquired using a Si-PIN photodiode detector to evaluate the performance of the machine learning in the nuclide analysis. The accuracy of the network training reached 90%. The evaluation confirmed that the trained neural network predicted the contribution of the five radionuclides within 26% on average.

articleTitle: Neutron Gamma Discrimination Performance with Plastic Scintillator According to SNR, Vertical Resolution and Sampling Frequency
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The hardware design of an acquisition chain for gamma neutron discrimination is based on trade-offs between a large number of parameters. This paper describes the influence of the resolution, sampling frequency and Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) of a digitizer on the performance of neutron gamma discrimination with EJ276 plastic scintillator. Thus, the study can help the user to select an adapted combination between these three parameters to obtain a good discrimination performance. The obtained results show that the SNR has the most important impact on the minimum sampling frequency required to perform the discrimination. The frequency can be reduced to 250 MHz if the SNR is higher than 4.

articleTitle: GEANT4 Surface Model for Background Radiation in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: GEANT4 is widely used to simulate radiation environments, yet in order to simulate environmental radiation scenarios complex background radiation must be considered. Given volumetric source distributions and attenuation considerations, providing a representative background can be computationally expensive. This work aims to reduce computational costs while staying faithful to the complex nature of the environment by developing a surface distributional model parameterised by reduced full volume simulations. Volume models for various γ energies transported through common media are characterised. Custom probability distributions are created for a triangulated surface for output energy, position and angular distribution. The current model has been developed and tested using Python, with a final implementation intended for use within the GEANT4 Particle Gun class. Results for the 1460 keV γ spectral line simulated within concrete are used to demonstrate and validate the technique against the underlying GEANT4 models. A simulation of complex surface emissions from NORM radiation sources within concrete, granite and soil, simulated within GEANT4 was presented.

articleTitle: Multilevel Modelling of Parkinson’s Disease Symptom Progression in 123I FP-CIT SPECT
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder. It is due to the reduction in the neurotransmitter dopamine by the loss of dopamine neurons. Thanks to new high-precision markers, it is possible to study PD before the development of symptoms and thus to model the progression of the disease. In this study, we apply a non-linear decomposition of 123I FP-CIT SPECT imaging in order to unveil the sources of variability, and relate them to symptomatology and disease progression. Isomap was compared to PCA, and multi-level modelling was used to assess the relation of the resulting composite imaging features and different symptomatology biomarkers and neuropsychological scales. The main source of variability was found to be the intensity at the striata, significantly linked to progression scales such as UPDRS or SCOPA. On the other hand, the modelling found additional sources of variance related to rigidity, tremor or other relevant symptoms.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Prototype of a Low-dose Stationary Tomographic Molecular Breast Imaging Camera Using 3D Position Sensitive CZT Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: A novel Molecular Breast Imaging system (MBI) is being developed by Kromek and University College London. MBI systems have been shown to provide excellent results in patients with dense breasts, but higher than mammography patient dose and long imaging time of 40 min impede their wide adoption. The design is based on a pair of opposing CZT detector arrays and high-density multi-pinhole (MPH) collimators. The new system combines superior energy and position resolution and depth of interaction (DOI) sensing of CZT detectors, wide range angular sampling of MPH collimators and novel de-multiplexing image reconstruction techniques to deliver tomographic images with stationary detectors. The new system is expected to mitigate the MBI drawbacks without compromising diagnostic content.Following the initial evaluation, a new feasibility prototype using upgraded ASIC and new front-end electronics was designed, built, and characterised. New image reconstruction and de-noising algorithms were developed on simulated data to improve the Contrast-to-Noise (CNR) ratio and reduce the fluctuations in the correlated background noise associated with MPH image reconstruction. The collimator geometry was further optimised by including non-local means noise filtering which increased the CNR by almost a factor of 3. The current results indicate that we can achieve the dose reduction to the mammography level, reduce the minimum size of detected lesions to about 6 mm and have an additional potential for reduction of the measurement time.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Detector Performances of New Thin Position-Sensitive Scintillation Detectors for SENJU Diffractometer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: A new thin position-sensitive scintillation neutron detectors have been developed to replace present scintillation detectors in SENJU diffractometer at J-PARC MLF. The SENJU diffractometer originally composed of 37 position-sensitive detectors, where each detector has neutron sensitive area of 256 × 256 mm with a pixel size of 4 × 4 mm. To renew some original detectors the new detectors have been developed based on <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>Li:ZnS scintillator and wavelength-shifting fibers technology. The developed replacement detectors were designed with a thin thickness of 12 cm, which is 40% of the original detector. The new detectors have also improved detector performances to the original ones in terms of detection efficiency (~60% for 2-Å neutrons) and count uniformity (5~8%). The produced six detector modules have been implemented to the beamline after checking their detector performances with a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">252</sup>Cf source. All the detectors have been operated in stable for a couple of months in the beamline. The background count rates were measured 200~350 1/hr/detector, which are consistent with the data measured in the laboratory.

articleTitle: A Direct Proof of Katsevich’s Algorithm in 2D Case
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this work, we propose a direct proof of Katsevich’s algorithm in two-dimensional (2D) case where the proof starts off directly from the 2D fan-beam projection data. Our proof connects the fan-beam data to the Fourier data directly. The geometric meaning in our approach manifests Tuy’s condition. During the proof, we identify that the 2D version of Katsevich’s algorithm is valid for a broader class of scanning trajectories. Also, during the proof, we identity that the so-called filtered backprojection (FBP) algorithm along π-lines comes out of Katsevich’s algorithm very naturally in 2D case.

articleTitle: Noise-to-noise Model Training for Noise Reduction in PET Imaging using Multiple Image Reconstructions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Recovery of the underlying signals and reducing the noise in PET imaging is critical since high levels of noise would hinder accurate qualitative and quantitative analysis. Due to the fact that noise-free data is not available in clinical studies (patent study), noise-to-noise model training frameworks could be employed which does not require noise-free reference data. This work set out to propose a multiple image reconstructions approach for the implementation of the noise-to-noise deep learning training in whole-body imaging. In noise-to-noise approaches, two noisy versions of the same input image are created to train the denoising model. Different noise realization could be achieved through multiple reconstructions of the same raw data in PET imaging. A deep learning model with three input channels was developed to take two auxiliary PET images (dedicatedly reconstructed for the task of noise-to-noise training) together with a smoothed version of the input PET image. The same input PET image is then employed as the target for the training of the model. The noise reduction capability of the proposed noise-to-noise framework (referred to as MRNN) was compared versus Gaussian, Bilateral, and non-local mean (NLM) post-reconstruction filters. The noise-to-noise deep learning model was trained and evaluated using eighty and twenty-five clinical whole-body FDG PET images. Regarding the clinical studies, the proposed noise-to-noise approach exhibited superior performance compared to the post-reconstruction de-noising filters. The quantitative bias in the denoised images reduced from 12.1% to -3.1% and -2.3% within the hot spots (or malignant lesions) when Gaussian, NLM, and MRNN methods were applied (p-value<0.03), respectively. Furthermore, regarding the SNR index, MRNN exhibited superior performance with SNR of 54.2 while Gaussian filter led to a SNR of 37.2 and NLM resulted in a SNR of 52.1. The proposed noise-to-noise approach based on the multiple PET image reconstructions exhibited superior de-noising capacity in comparison to the conventional post-reconstruction denoising approaches. The proposed noise-to-noise could be exploited when a noise-free dataset, such as clinical SPECT and PET studies, is not available.

articleTitle: Developments Regarding the Integration of FPGA RDMA into the ATLAS Readout with FELIX in High Luminosity LHC
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) is used by the ATLAS experiment at CERN in the new readout system based on FELIX (Front-End Link eXchange) for its networking layer. The FELIX system is used to interface the front-end electronics to commodity hardware in the server farm. In the current implementation of FELIX, RDMA communication is implemented using software on both ends of the RDMA links. FELIX is using RDMA through RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) to transmit data from its servers to the Software Readout Driver devices in the server farm using off-the-shelf networking equipment. As a consequence of the High Luminosity LHC upgrade, improvements in the data throughput will be needed. These improvements can be achieved by implementing RDMA support in the FELIX FPGA to simplify the path the data is taking through the readout system. This FPGA implementation of the RDMA protocol has been developed and tested. Now, a version of FELIX that uses this implementation is being proposed and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Spatial Resolution Enhancement and Hardware Upgrade in XSpectra® Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The necessity to guarantee higher and higher quality standards in the food market, requires the real-time inspection technologies adopted on food production lines to continuously be improved, in order to be able to detect foreign bodies of even more challenging dimensions and materials. Xnext patented technology XSpectra<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> has already successfully entered the food market sector providing breakthrough performances, but, as required by the increasing market demands, the technology is under constant enhancement. A first improvement we have implemented consists in reducing the pixel area from 0.8 × 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 0.4 × 0.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, thus ensuring an higher spatial resolution. Moreover, additional improvements can be introduced by properly optimizing the operating parameters of the detector itself according to its working point. The eye of the technology is in fact a detector made of Cadmium Telluride (CdTe), a material that, as well known in literature, suffers from both polarization effects as well as time-instabilities, especially when operated at the extremely high photon fluxes required by our application. Here we report the experimental results obtained with our 0.4 mm detector prototype as well as the improvements obtained, in real operating conditions, with an hardware-optimized version of the detector.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Programmable Delay Line IP-Core based on Digital-to-Time Converter for FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this paper, we are going to present a Digital-to-Time Delay-line (DTC-DL) IP-Core, capable of detecting the rising edge of an asynchronous and aperiodic input signal, and replicating it at its output, with a dynamically programmable delay. This solution is compatible with Xilinx 28-nm 7-Series Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) and System-on-Chip (SOC) devices. Compared to Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) solutions, the one proposed in this work features high flexibility, low hardware overhead, and, in particular, re-programmability; which makes the IP-Core adaptable to many applications and, above all, upgradable without a complete redesign of the system. The DTC-DL is based on the concept of Nutt-Interpolation, combining a synchronous Coarse Logic and an asynchronous Fine Logic. This interpolation allows to have both a resolution in the order of tens of picoseconds, and maximum delay of hundreds of milliseconds. The output jitter is kept below a few tens of picoseconds r.m.s. thanks to an architecture using only one IDELAY primitive instance per channel, calibrated thanks to the IDELAYCTRL primitive, which is given by Xilinx. The DTC-DL IP-Core has been successfully validated on a custom board entirely developed at Politecnico di Milano, hosting a Xilinx Artix-7 XC7A100TFTG256-2.

articleTitle: Real-time Voxel-Wise Patient-Specific Monte Carlo Dose Reconstruction in Total Body CT Scan Images using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) dose measurement is an essential step toward dose optimization. Available dosimetry tools such as pre-tabulated software, e.g., Radimetric, are available but not as accurate as direct Monte-Carlo (MC) calculations. However, MC approaches suffer from heavy computational burden. This study aimed to develop a model to directly predict the radiation dose maps from CT images employing deep neural networks. Forty-eight total body CT images were included. The ground truth voxel dose map was calculated using MC calculation (MCNPX) . CT images were cropped, normalized, and then fed to a residual deep neural network to predict the voxel dose map. Our method was evaluated by quantitative parameters of relative error (RE), relative absolute error (RAE), structural similarity index (SSIM), and gamma pass rate. Multiple organs were segmented, and the organ dose was compared between the ground truth and deep predicted dose maps. The average SSIM, RE, RAE, and gamma pass rate were 0.96± 0.01, 3.43±3.29, 5.17±2.73, and 91.4±3.4, respectively. Also, the average absolute error in organ dose was less than 7 percent, while the highest error was in the lungs. This proposed method can produce the dose maps with acceptable accuracy in less than seconds. Using this model the real-time, patient-specific dose can be measured in the clinical situation.

articleTitle: Materials and Defects Characterization of CdZnTe Sensors using the Inverse Synthesis Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Room Temperature Semiconductor Radiation Detectors are of high interest in nuclear imaging. However, the manufacture of these semiconductors can generate some defects in the material that compromise the performance of the sensors. In this research, we will characterize the transport properties and defects of CdZnTe detectors using a novel Inverse Synthesis method.

articleTitle: Camera-based Motion Correction for PET/MR Brain Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this work, we evaluated the performance of a camera-based rigid body motion correction solution in PET studies. We compared the image quality obtained by reconstructing a static phantom scan to those obtained by reconstructing a moving phantom scan with and without applying motion correction. Our suggested solution uses a camera to track a 3D marker attached to the object to be imaged (in this work, a resolution phantom). This data was incorporated in the multiple acquisition frames (MAF) image reconstruction algorithm to compensate for motion. While we got multiple spatially shifted replicas of the resolution phantom in the motion study's reconstructed image when motion correction was not applied, the motion-corrected image was comparable to the static image, with some degradation in spatial resolution (3.2-4.2 vs. 2.8-3.2 mm) and lower peak to valley ratio (indicating lower contrast to noise ratio). The context of the results presented is in PET/MR imaging, but in principle, this motion compensation method could be used in any type of medical imaging modality.

articleTitle: X-ray Fluorescence Compton Imaging Technique Based on a Single-layer Timepix3 Photon-counting Detector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: X-ray fluorescence computed tomography (XFCT) is one of the most commonly used X-ray fluorescence imaging modalities. XFCT can provide molecular and functional information at a lower internal dose, which uses X-ray tubes to simulate X-ray fluorescence (XRF) photons. For XFCT, mechanical collimators are usually used to obtain the incident direction of photons, which will lead to the loss of detection efficiency. Compton camera (CC) is an imaging method without mechanical collimators, which can realize three-dimensional imaging with scanning in a single view. In this work, we present the first result of X-ray fluorescence Compton imaging. The proposed X-ray fluorescence Compton camera (XFCC) consists of a 150kVp X-ray tube and a Timepix3 photon-counting detector. When imaging with a 6mm diameter pipe filled with 100 mg/ml Gd solution, the maximum half width (FWHM) is about 12 mm.

articleTitle: Investigation of Different Multiplexing Strategies for Monolithic Detector with Monte Carlo Simulation and Cramer-Rao Lower Bound
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Monolithic gamma detector is gaining increasing interest due to its intrinsic DOI capability, lower cost and potentially better timing and energy resolution compared to conventional pixelated detector designs. In monolithic detector designs, it is preferable to perform a certain level of multiplexing to reduce the number of readout channels in real application. However, multiplexing comes with degradations of detector’s spatial resolution. The spatial resolution degradations under different multiplexing strategies need to be carefully evaluated. In this work, we studied the positioning performance of a monolithic gamma detector under different multiplexing strategies. The light response model (LRF) of the detector was generated with Monte Carlo simulation combined with experimentally calibrated energy response model. Based on the generated LRF, Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) was used to evaluate the detector positioning performance under no multiplexing and six different multiplexing strategies including RCS-12, Diagonal-11, Square-9, Corner-9, RCS-6 and RCS-GAP-6. The results demonstrate that there is only slight positioning performance degradation from no multiplexing to RCS-12 with the average value of square root of CRLB from 0.35 mm to 0.45 mm in x direction and from 0.53 mm to 0.71 mm in z direction. However, if the readout channel number is further reduced to 9 (Square-9 or Corner-9) and 6 (RCS-6 or RCS-GAP-6), significant positioning performance degradations are observed. The positioning performance of Diagonal-11 is much poorer than that of RCS-12 though only one readout channel fewer. To conclude, RCS-12 is a promising multiplexing strategy with reversed detector positioning capability compared to no multiplexing and similar multiplexing approach could be used in other monolithic gamma detector designs. This work provides practical guidance in choosing multiplexing strategy to facilitate monolithic detector design.

articleTitle: A Novel Attention-based Neural Network for Automated Lung Lesion Delineation from 4DCT Images
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Radiotherapy plays an important role in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer. Accurate segmentation of the gross target volume (GTV) is critical for successful radiotherapy delivery. Deep learning techniques are able to offer fast and accurate segmentation, which could serve as decision support for specialists and save time compared to manual delineation. Regarding the large the volume of the lung compared to the lung lesions, achieving lesion segmentation with very high accuracy is challenging due to the large input field. In this light, dedicated networks with attention modules are needed for automated and accurate lung lesion delineation. This work used a 3D-Unet equipped with a novel attention module to segment the gross tumor volume from 4D CT images presenting with non-small cell lung cancer. A total of 730 clinical 4DCT lung images were included in this study, 657 for training and 73 images for test. The proposed framework consists of two major components: attention and segmentation modules, wherein the attention module would estimate approximate location of the lung lesion through a coarse segmentation of the input image with high true-positive rate to ensure the inclusion of the entire lesion (using a dedicated loss function). The outcome of the attention module as well as the key feature maps from the decoder part are fed into the segmentation module. Given the restricted field provided by the attention module, the segmentation module would perform accurate/precise delineation of the lung lesion.The DSC, JSC and Hassdorf distance indices were used to evaluate our proposed method. Dice score increased from 0.75 to 0.83. Jac-card and Hausdorff distance indices also improved from 0.62 to 0.73, and from 4.29mm to 3.73mm, respectively. The proposed network, exhibited superior performance to the network without attention model.

articleTitle: Pixelated Energy-dispersive Photon-counting Detector Calibration with X-ray Diffraction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: X-ray photon counting detector (PCD) technology has brought great energy-resolved imaging ability into medical imaging applications such as spectral CT, X-ray fluorescence (XRF) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). However, practical factors such as statistical charge fluctuation, charge sharing and K-escape effect deforms detected spectrums. Accurate PCD energy response calibration is critical for spectrum restoration. Metal powder XRF is the most commonly used calibration method for PCD energy response in laboratories. However, XRF is limited by few discrete incident energies and relatively narrow energy range of easily-accessed metal materials. In this work, we proposed a new method for PCD energy response calibration based on crystal XRD.
