abstract: Convolutional neural networks have been widely proposed/developed to conduct efficient and accurate organ segmentation, wherein a variety of loss functions have been considered to achieve optimal organ detection from the input data. Despite extraordinary performance of neural networks, noticeable errors located at the boundary/proximity of the target organs are observed as well as outliers in the form of island of voxels or voids/holes within the solid/uniform part of the target. To address these issues, we set out to investigate an alternative semantic segmentation solution based on the distance map using the regression solutions. In the proposed framework the distance maps obtained from the target masks are directly considered as the target within the training of the model, wherein regression networks and loss functions are used for the development of the model. Since the distance maps are continuous-valued data (as opposed to binary masks) any regression solutions could be employed to achieve the segmentation of the target organ/lesion. To implement the regression-based segmentation framework, a residual neural network was trained using the conventional segmentation framework and a hybrid Jac-card/cross-entropy loss function and the distance map framework using an L2 loss function. These models were tested for kidney segmentation using the decathlon dataset. The regression-based approach outperformed the conventional deep learning-based segmentation method with statistically significant differences (p-values <0.05). In addition to the overall superior performance of the regression-based approach, this method led to no outliers in the form of islands of voxels or holes inside the target structure. However, the conventional segmentation approach resulted in 5 outliers out of 30 subjects in the test dataset. Moreover, owing to the fact that the segmentation problem is converted to a regression task, we employed an L2 loss function since this function would perform better if the training dataset were not noisy compared to the L1 loss function. We intentionally added some noise and wrong samples to the training dataset and repeated the training. In this case, the L1 loss function led to better results than the L2 loss function. This would be regarded as an advantage of the proposed framework that the regression loss function with specific properties could be employed for the segmentation tasks. Overall, this study demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed regression-based solution over the conventional deep learning segmentation approach.

articleTitle: Anatomy-Guided Synthesis of Novel CT Images at Full Hounsfield Range
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this work, we present an approach that can synthesize novel CT images across the full Hounsfield range using a very small annotated dataset of around thirty patients and a large non-annotated dataset with high resolution medical images. Our method uses these two datasets in a sequence of steps involving texture learning via StyleGAN and semi-supervised learning via CycleGAN to generate a large annotated medical dataset suitable for use in deep learning algorithms for medical applications. Using an anatomy exploration interface we can then generate CT images with anatomies that were non-existent within either of the datasets, without compromising accuracy and quality. We show that our approach works for all Hounsfield windows with minimal depreciation in anatomical plausibility.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Complimentary Rebinning Reconstruction for Off-Center Flat Panel Detector CBCT Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Off-center flat panel detectors have been utilized in CBCT imaging to obtain a larger field of view such as the thoracic and upper abdomen regions. As a compromise, truncation artifacts arising from the asymmetrical geometry further degrades the image that is already commonly affected by motion-induced artifacts. Apart from the common iterative reconstruction methods, analytical-based reconstruction using projection weighting (PW)-based methods are commonly adopted to mitigate the truncation artifact via applying a weighting function on the doubly acquired redundant projection data. However, the disadvantage is the occurrence of an overall image intensity bias due to the missing data in the truncated projection region. Therefore, this work proposes evaluates the utilization of a modified complimentary rebinning (CR) approach as an alternative mitigation method while preserving the overall intensity of the reconstructed image. Using the recently developed MRI-based 4D CBCT digital phantom, five datasets are simulated based on the half-fan geometry to assess the performance of both PW and CR methods. The results indicated that CR effectively removes the truncation artifact with a significantly lower root mean squared error value at 0.18%, compared to PW at 0.51% (P=0.00). The evaluation of the scaling factor between the reconstructed and ground truth images indicated a reduction of half of the original overall intensity in PW with a mean value at 2.03, in contrast to CR at 1.01. Finally, using the tissue interface sharpness metric to quantify motion blur, no significant difference was found between PW and CR (P=0.23), even though CR displayed a higher value at 0.94 compared to PW at 0.90. This shows that the proposed CR method is able to produce an image with the same sharpness quality compared to the common PW in effectively mitigating truncation artifacts while preserving the overall intensity of the reconstructed image.

articleTitle: Generation of Photon Attenuation Corrected PET From MRI and Uncorrected PET Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this work, we evaluate the feasibility of a simplified approach of performing MR-based attenuation correction (MRAC) by generating AC PET images directly from non-attenuation corrected (NAC) PET and MR images using a machine learning model known as conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). We evaluate this approach for the head and neck region of a PET/MR and PET/CT dataset. We trained and tested a model converting MR Dixon Water, MR Dixon Fat, and NAC PET (multi-channel input) to AC PET. Our model achieved a mean pixel value difference of 2.06% in the head and neck region, NRMSE of 1.29%, PSNR of 37.55, and SSIM of 0.97 compared to the true AC PET images determined by CT-based attenuation correction. These metrics are a large improvement compared to the NAC PET images which had a mean pixel value difference of 5.35%, NRMSE of 3.27%, PSNR of 28.80, and SSIM of 0.85 when comparing to AC PET.

articleTitle: Electrical Results of the ATLAS ITk Pre-production Stave at Brookhaven National Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is currently preparing to upgrade the current inner tracking detector with a new all-silicon Inner Tracker, the ITk. This new detector will be made of five inner Pixel layers and four outer Strip layers. The building blocks of the ITk strip barrel layers are the staves. A stave is made of a low-mass support structure which hosts the common electrical, optical and cooling services as well as 28 silicon modules, 14 on each side. After an extensive prototyping phase, all the ITk institutes are currently in pre-production, moving towards production. In this contribution we outline the challenging aspects encountered during the stave pre-production testing phase at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL). In particular, the electrical characterization of the latest pre-production stave built at BNL in late 2022 will be discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Automatic Segmentation of Prostate and its Anatomical Sub-regions from MR Images using a Novel ResUnet Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides detailed anatomical images of the prostate and its anatomical sub-regions for radiation treatment planning. Automated segmentation of the prostate and its sub-regions from MR images facilitates prostate cancer diagnostic and treatment planning. In addition, the identification of the whole prostate gland, the distinction between the central gland (CG) and the peripheral gland (PZ) would enable differentiate diagnosis since the risk of cancer varies in these zones. However, their boundaries are often very vague and blurred in anatomical images. This work will present a ResUnet model for accurate regional segmentation of the prostate zones from magnetic resonance (MR) images. The focus would be on the segmentation of the whole prostate gland (WG), central gland (CG), and peripheral zone (PZ) from T2-weighted MR images, where PZ+CG=WG. A novel ResUnet model was proposed and trained using 81 clinical datasets and evaluated on 35 subjects undergone T2-weighted MR imaging from 6 different centers. The performance of the proposed segmentation model was compared with the conventional Unet model with the same number of trainable parameters. The ResUnet model with ISBI13 dataset achieved the whole prostate, central zone, and peripheral zone delineation with maximum Dice indices of 89.93±1.0, 91.56±2.0, and 89.04±2.5, respectively. While the Unet model with the same dataset exhibited inferior performance compared to the proposed ResUnet model with maximum Dice indices of 88.75±1.1, 89.81±2.2, and 77.25±3.5 for the whole prostate, central zone, and peripheral zone, respectively. The quantitative analysis of the segmentation results exhibited the superior performance of the proposed ResUnet model over the conventional Unet model. This model could be employed for automated prostate (as well as its sub-regions) segmentation to reduce the workload in the diagnosis of prostate cancer.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Range Verification in Proton Therapy Based on Neutron Information
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Proton therapy has been widely used in tumor therapy due to its Bragg peak characteristics. However, the uncertainty of proton range will seriously affect the therapeutic effect. Therefore, it is important to explore the proton real-time range verification technology. In this paper, we investigate the feasibility of range verification based on detection of secondary neutrons produced in nuclear interaction during proton therapy. Firstly, the neutron detection system based on EJ276 plastic scintillator is established, which can detect neutrons from most directions. Then, the energy and flux information of secondary neutrons produced in phantom are simulated and analyzed. The variation of neutron flux is related to proton range. At last, the neutrons direction and position recorded in detector are utilized to trace the neutron emission position to obtain the traced neutron flux distribution (TNFD). The results demonstrated that the distal drop of the TNFD is close to proton range.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Aided Motion Estimation for Dynamic Brain PET
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Here we present initial work to develop a PET data driven motion correction method which uses a deep learning (DL) model to aid in the motion estimation during the tracer uptake period when the tracer spatial distribution changes rapidly and images generally contain very few functional/anatomical landmarks. Data from three different tracers were used ([<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup>C]RAC, [<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F]FDG, and [<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup>C]PBR) to form a representative dataset of 40 motion-free brain scans. The dataset was used to train and test a model capable of mapping 1-second, low-count frames acquired during the initial uptake period to their corresponding 1-minute, higher-count frame containing better structural features than the original low-count frames. The ability to recover a known motion trace that was artificially injected into subject data during initial tracer uptake was verified. The use of the DL model reduced the motion estimation error from 6 mm and 3 degrees (when registration was performed without the aid of DL) to 1 mm and 2 degrees.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Volumetric Positioning of High Energy Photons in Monolithic Crystals for Positron Emission Tomography
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this work we employ simulations to calibrate the positioning algorithm and determine its error for a Lutetium– Yttrium Oxyorthosilicate monolithic crystal (LYSO)-based position emission tomography (PET) scanner. Using the centre of gravity method, with a bias, to extract position of photoelectric interactions, we measure the standard deviation of estimated position (x, y and depth) from true position. Finally, we simulate a point source scan with the system. The resulting data are processed and reconstructed using Software for Tomographic Image Reconstruction (STIR) with depth encoding. We found that introducing bias decreases standard deviation for X, Y position within a monolithic crystal from "2.62 mm" to "1.81 mm".

articleTitle: Conceptual Design of a Dual-Panel Dedicated Prostate PET Scanner: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Cost-effective dedicated PET scanners for prostate cancer imaging providing high-quality functional images are highly desirable for efficient monitoring of suspicious patients. In this light, this work set out to introduce ProVision, a state-of-the-art dedicated PET imager. ProVision is an open gantry, dual-panel PET scanner with four layers of detection modules offering an excellent depth of detection capability and high spatial resolution. A Monte Carlo simulation study was adopted to assess the spatial resolution of the ProVision PET scanner in comparison with the general-purpose Biograph mCT PET/CT scanner (Siemens, Healthcare). The spatial resolution of the ProVision was measured using the NEMA protocol consisting of six point-sources with diameters of 1 mm located at 10, 50, and 60 mm off-center along the X, Y, and Z axes. Image reconstruction was implemented in a fully 3D fashion using a maximum likelihood expectation-maximization algorithm, wherein in projection space, each sinogram plane is of 224 (detector bins) × 90 (angular views). In the X-Y plane, the ProVision PET scanner exhibited superior spatial resolution with a full width half maximum (FWHM) of about 2.7 mm compared to the mCT PET scanner with FWHM of about 3.1 mm. The improved spatial resolution could be attributed to the excellent DOI capability of the ProVision PET scanner owing to the four-layer detector towers. A degraded spatial resolution was observed along the Z-axis for the ProVision PET scanner owing to the limited angle coverage of this scanner which leads to elongation along the Z-axis. Shift variant and anisotropic point spread function modelling is proposed to compensate for the spatial resolution degradation along the Z-axis. The preliminary results indicate that the ProVision PET scanner has a great potential for high-resolution functional imaging of the prostate.

articleTitle: Calibration of the SOlar Neutron TRACking (SONTRAC) Instrument
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Solar neutrons are a secondary product of the interaction of trapped flare-accelerated charged particles with the dense chromospheric plasma. As they are electromagnetically neutral, solar neutrons and γ-rays may escape the corona and serve as probes to study flare-accelerated particles and processes that are otherwise inaccessible. However, neutrons are challenging to detect both due to high ambient backgrounds of Earth-orbiting spacecraft, and the short lifetime of free neutrons. Neutrons are traditionally measured using a time-of-flight technique requiring measurements in two detectors separated by a relatively large distance. Using this technique, measurements of fast (>0.5 MeV) neutrons require large instruments that are challenging to fly on space-constrained spacecraft. The SOlar Neutron TRACking (SONTRAC) instrument is a compact, imaging neutron spectrometer composed of orthogonally-stacked planes of scintillating optical fibers read out by miniature silicon photomultipliers (SiPM). Ionization tracks of recoil protons produced by neutron interactions within the fibers provide information to allow reconstruction of the energy and direction of incident neutrons. In this work, we discuss recent calibration efforts of SONTRAC, highlighting measurements of mono-energetic protons and neutrons at the Crocker Nuclear Laboratory at UC Davis as well as complimentary Monte Carlo modeling of the instrument. These measurements and simulations were utilized to compute conversion factors from instrumental units to physically meaningful values using the well-understood behavior of proton ionization behavior through material, and improve our understanding of the instrument response. Calibration efforts in preparation for the accelerator run are also presented.

articleTitle: The Phase-I Upgrade of the ATLAS Level-1 Calorimeter Trigger
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The ATLAS Level-1 Calorimeter Trigger (L1Calo) is a hardware-based system that identifies events containing calorimeter-based physics objects, including electrons, photons, taus, jets, and missing transverse energy. L1Calo underwent a significant programme of upgrades for Run 3 of the LHC which is running at higher energies and instantaneous luminosity. The existing hardware will be replaced by a new system of FPGA-based feature extractor (FEX) modules, which processes finer-granularity information from the calorimeters and executes more sophisticated algorithms to identify physics objects; these upgrades permit better performance in a challenging high-luminosity and high-pileup environment. The features of the upgraded L1Calo system are introduced and the current status of installation and commissioning is described. In addition, the expected performance of L1Calo in Run 3 is discussed.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Bayesian DIP Denoising as a Preprocessing Step for Kinetic Modelling in Dynamic PET
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Noise (among other artefacts) could be considered to be the bane of PET. Many methods have been proposed to alleviate the worst annoyances of noise, however, not many take into account the temporal nature of dynamically acquired PET. Here, we propose an adaption of a method, which has seen increasing attention in more traditional imaging denoising circles. Deep Image Prior exploits the initialisation of a carefully designed neural network, so as to treat it as a bank of custom filters, which are to be trained and used afresh on each new image, independently. Deep Image Prior has seen adaptation to PET previously (including dynamic PET), however, many of these adaptations do not take into account the large memory requirements of the method. Additionally, most previous work does not address the main weakness of the Deep Image Prior, its stopping criteria. Here, we propose a method which is both memory efficient, and includes a smoothing regularisation. In addition, we provide uncertainty estimates by incorporating a Bayesian approximation (using dropout), and prototype a training scheme by which the model is fit on all data simultaneously. The denoised images are then used as input for kinetic modelling. To evaluate the method, dynamic XCAT simulations have been produced, with a field of view of the lung and liver. The results of the new methods (along with total variation and the old Deep Image Prior) have been compared by; a visual analysis, SSIM, and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> values. Results indicate that the new methods potentially outperform the old methods, without increasing computation time, while reducing system requirements.

articleTitle: Multi-tracer Deep Learning for PET Head Motion Correction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Head motion during brain positron emission tomography (PET) image acquisition decreases image quality and increases quantification errors. So far, no robust approach allows continuous head motion tracking without using an external device. In this feasibility study, we propose a multi-tracer deep learning head motion correction (mDL-HMC) model to predict rigid head motion based on supervised learning of gold-standard camera motion tracking. mDL-HMC utilizes a novel feature-wise transformation block to condition the network to different tracer types. Quantitative and qualitative results from five subjects demonstrate that training this model with combined data from two different tracers (FDG and UCB-J) improves motion correction performance compared to single-tracer models. Our head motion correction results have the potential to eliminate the need for external motion tracking hardware.

articleTitle: Design of HPSoC – a 10GSa/s Waveform Digitizer for Readout of Dense Sensor Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this article we describe the design of the HPSoC, a multi-channel waveform digitizing and processing Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) to readout fast and dense sensor arrays (e.g. LGADs). The chip will be able to service up to 100 channels, for bidimensional sensor arrays with a pitch of down to 300 um, operate with 10 GSa/s waveform digitization and use autonomous triggering, feature extraction and multichannel data fusion. In this paper, we present the architecture design, and the design and fabrication of a prototype with 4 channels to validate the components.

articleTitle: Self-Normalization for a 1-Millimeter Resolution Clinical PET System Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In positron emission tomography, normalization is an image correction process that normalizes the coincidence event sensitivities of each line-of-response (LOR). This work proposes an end-to-end, conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN)-based self-normalization using Pix2Pix. We simulated ten voxelized phantoms with SimSET and acquired 15,200 image pairs. The results show that, when comparing synthetically normalized images with respect to target images, the mean values of PSNR, NRMSE, and SSIM for the images that were acquired for ≥10 OSEM iterations were 22.3, 0.38, and 0.73, respectively, which were 46.8%, 55.6%, and 56.1% improvements compared to those of unnormalized images, respectively. The mean values of NRMSE (ROI) and SSIM (ROI) of the images were 0.15 and 0.92, respectively, which were 73.1% and 59.1% improvements against unnormalized slices, respectively. The mean value of NCRC of the images was 0.84, and the CNR of the predicted images was 2.81, which were 63.8% and 113.5% gains against those of unnormalized images, respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Digital Tracking Calorimeter for In-Situ Range Verification during Particle Therapy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: When protons or heavier ions are used for radiation treatment, it is paramount to assure quality by performing range verification during or right after treatment. This work presents, for the first time, a feasibility study for proton therapy range verification based on secondary charged particles using the digital tracking calorimeter designed by the Bergen pCT collaboration. Additionally, we compare the precision achievable with protons and carbon ions, by applying regression models to predict the beam range with Monte Carlo-simulated data. The simulated treatment scenario contains a water cuboid phantom of different thicknesses, with protons and carbon ions as treatment modality at different medically relevant energy levels. Results show that the error for carbon ions is lower despite having 100 times fewer primaries simulated, due to the much higher readout yield. The lowest mean absolute error was observed with a kernel regression as 0.27 ± 0.04 mm for protons, and with a Gaussian process as 0.18 ± 0.02 mm for carbon ions, which shows feasibility of range verification for proton and carbon therapy based on charged secondary particles using the digital tracking calorimeter.

articleTitle: Modeling Physics and Electronics to Study the Coincidence Time Resolution of a CZT PET System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This work summarizes simulation efforts to model a preclinical high-resolution cadmium zinc telluride positron emission tomography scanner using Geant4 Applications for Emission Tomography along with post-processing modeling of charge carrier transport and experimentally relevant readout electronics. The model intended to characterize degradative elements of the system’s coincidence time resolution. The experimental system being modeled here consists of two panels composed of an 8 x 3 array of 39 x 39 x 10 mm3 detector modules. Each detector module contains two cadmium zinc telluride crystals with 39 anode strips and 38 steering electrode strips on one side and 8 cathode strips orthogonal to the anodes on the other. The two crystals in each module are stacked and arranged in an anode-cathode-cathode-anode order. From Geant4 Applications for Emission Tomography, idealized HITS data were recorded and further processed in MATLAB to include a charge transport model, which allowed the current induced on the electrodes to be calculated. This induced current was then passed through slow and fast shapers to model the system readout of both the energy and the pick off time of each event respectively. From this first iteration of the model, the resulting coincidence time spectrum gave a coincidence time resolution (CTR) of 153 ns FWHM, while previous experimental results reported 210 ns. The dominant factor limiting the CTR is the contribution from cathode energy dependent time walk from the parameters that are analyzed here.

articleTitle: A Portable Fully Digital Dosimeter for Pulsed Radiation Fields
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Realtime sampling of pulses generated in radiation detectors is a standard technology in stationary experiments for high energy and nuclear physics. Additionally, mobile applications and especially dosimetry can benefit from the data conserved in such technology. The full digitalization of a pulse of an organic scintillator conserves a large amount of information. In the current work, it is shown how realtime analyses of sampled pulses contribute to advanced and accurate dosimetry. Especially in pulsed radiation fields the time structure can be conserved and the time structure can be used to identify time modulated radiation sources. Additionally, a tissue equivalent detector material assures a proper dose weighting in pile-up situations. A portable device is presented which measures ambient as well as directional dose for photons in the range from 15 keV to 1.3 MeV and has shown an accuracy of better than 5 % in pulsed reference x-ray fields at the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt in Brunswick, Germany. Details of the sampling and analysis algorithms are presented and how conservation of time information can be exploited.

articleTitle: Compact Design of an FPGA Based Data Acquisition (DAQ) System for an RF-penetrable TOF-PET Brain Dedicated Insert
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: With advanced PET system development, processing a high number of channels online is necessary and critical, especially for applications with one-to-one coupled crystals and silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs). We are developing an RF-penetrable TOF-PET brain dedicated insert with lutetiumyttrium oxyorthosilicate (LYSO) crystals one-to-one coupled to SiPMs. There are 768 crystal-SiPM channels per detector module, and a PET insert ring comprises 16 detector modules. A compact design to process 12288 channels with a designed 20 kcps singles count rate per channel in real-time is challenging. In this paper, we developed an FPGA-based data acquisition (DAQ) system using a commercial evaluation board and characterized its performance with two full detector modules; each having 768 crystal-SiPM channels. We achieved a global energy resolution of 11.46 ± 0.02% FWHM and a global coincidence time resolution of 224.47 ± 0.15ps FWHM over 1536 SiPM-crystal channels with DAQ online processing. All parameters including global energy resolution, global CTR, coincidence count rate, and random count rate changed less than 3% between offline processing and online DAQ processing.

articleTitle: Photoneutron Detection with Small Organic Glass Scintillators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Photon active interrogation is a promising technique to detect illicit special nuclear material, relying upon high-energy photons to induce photofission and (γ, n) reactions in nuclear material. However, the photon sources used in active interrogation are very intense and it can be difficult to detect the neutron signatures due to the high photon background. The intense radiation environment can overwhelm <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>He-based detectors and result in pulse pile-up in pulse-shape-discrimination-capable detectors, degrading particle classification. To reduce pulse pileup effects, we use small (6-mm) stilbene and organic glass scintillators (OGS) to reduce the efficiency such that pile-up becomes relatively rare, and detectors are shielded in a lead cave. In this work, we use a 9-MeV bremsstrahlung source to induce photonuclear reactions in depleted uranium and measure the neutron emissions using the two detector arrays. To improve measurement fidelity, we expand the array from two detectors to four and increase measurement time. We then briefly compare the performance of the stilbene and organic glass scintillators during photon irradiation of depleted uranium. Performance metrics include pile-up rate and neutron count rate. With the stilbene array, we measure a net increase of 146 ± 13 neutrons in 2 hours produced by the depleted uranium, and with the OGS array, we measure a net increase of 242 ± 18 neutrons in 2 hours. Although measurement results suggest that the OGS has superior neutron efficiency, the elevated neutron count rate is most likely caused by pile-up misclassification. Future work will explore the use of silicon photomultipliers instead of photomultiplier tubes and employ more rigorous pile-up rejection.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Noise and Low Background Charge Sensitive Amplifier for the Readout of Germanium Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The observation of neutrinoless double beta decay would have major implications in the understanding of the origin of the matter in the universe. Given zero electric charge and no colour, they may be Majorana particles, i.e. their own antiparticles. The Large Enriched Germanium Experiment for Neutrinoless double beta Decay (LEGEND) is a ton-scale experimental program to search for the neutrinoless decay in the isotope <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76</sup>Ge. In this framework, we have designed a new ASIC in the 0.35 µm CMOS technology, which will fulfill Ge-detector requirements. The ASIC has a key role in order to obtain a good energy resolution and a high radiopurity environment that are crucial conditions in neutrinoless double beta decay experiments. The ASIC has been designed featuring a low noise Charge Sensitive Amplifier (CSA) and an on-chip Low-DropOut regulator (LDO). The LDO allows the chip to be powered without bypass capacitors which are not compliant with the radiopurity requirement. With a 50 pA leakage current and a detector capacitance of 4 pF, the ASIC shows a noise performance of 50 ${\text{e}}_{rms}^ - $. In this work, we also present the simulated transient response of the CSA. In the end a dedicated Line Driver circuit drives the signal in a differential way over a distance of about 10 m.

articleTitle: One and Two Poles Compensation of Charge Sensitive Amplifiers with Resistive Feedback to Improve the Energy Resolution in GRETA
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The Gamma Ray Energy Tracking Array (GRETA) is a detector system currently under construction in the US. The energy of the gamma-ray is determined in real time inside field programmable gate arrays (FPGA), employing the typical processing chain of shaper, pole-zero cancellation (PZC), baseline restoration and pulse high analysis. In this paper we propose a 2-poles PZC for GRETA based on the analysis of the charge sensitive amplifier (CSA). We derive the time and discrete domain versions of the PZC, and implemented it using floating point and integer math. We then compare the performance of 1- and 2-poles PZC for a detector and different gamma-ray rates. We observed an improvement on the full width half maximum energy (FWHM) resolution of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co 1.33 MeV line at 90 Kgammas/s for the 2-poles PZC in relation to a 1-pole PZC. Finally, we describe how the 2-pole PZC can be implemented inside an FPGA and meet the high computational rate required for GRETA.

articleTitle: Development of a Simultaneous Photon Counting and Energy Integrating Readout ASIC for X-ray Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a photon counting and charge integrating readout ASIC for semiconductor detectors for X-ray imaging applications. The information of photon counts and energy integration can be obtained simultaneously from one detector. Photon counting will be used at low to medium rate to get rid of electronics noise and to improve the dose efficiency with optimum energy weights. While the energy integrating will be used at high rate when the photon counts start to be saturated and hence large dynamic range can be achieved. The integration of both photon counting and energy integrating channels is achieved by the introduction of the charge pump circuits.The readout ASIC consists of 128 signal processing channels and the periphery circuits. Each channel integrates photon counting mode energy integrating mode. The photon counting mode circuit consists of a charge sensitive preamplifier, a CR-RC shaper, two discriminators, two 15-bit photon-counters. The energy integrating mode circuit consists of the charge sensitive preamplifier shared with the counting channel, the charge pump circuit, the correlated double sampling circuit and a Wilkinson ADC. A local 24bit-register chain is also integrated into each pixel for calibration, gain and baseline tuning and selection of different working modes, which can be programmed through an SPI slow control interface. More design details and test results will be discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Deep Learning-based Attenuation Correction in the Image Domain for 68Ga-PSMA PET Imaging using Artifact-free Dataset
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: One of the image quality degradation factors in PET imaging is photon attenuation, wherein the presence of an attenuation map is critical for the task of Attenuation Correction (AC). Different approaches have been proposed to address the lack of standard transmission or CT scans in PET imaging, particularly deep learning-based algorithms to correct attenuation and scatter directly in the image domain without the need for anatomical images. However, artifacts in the PET CT-AC images like the respiration motion, halo, or truncation artifacts would decrease the accuracy of the model training. In this work a novel approach was followed to detect artifact corrupted PET-CT images (where PET-CT images are regarded as reference for model training for the task of AC). Then, the PET-CT images with artifact were removed from the training dataset to create a clean dataset. In the next iteration, the clean dataset was used to train a deep learning model to perform AC in the image domain without requiring anatomical images. The proposed framework was evaluated for AC in whole-body 68Ga-PSMA PET imaging. The artifact-free trained network exhibited lower voxel-wise values of mean error (-0.009±0.43 SUV) and mean absolute error (0.09±0.41 SUV) in comparison with the trained network with unclean dataset. The evaluation on external validation dataset before and after cleaning the training dataset demonstrated the improved AC performance due to the application of the proposed data purification framework. The training of the model before and after cleaning the training dataset demonstrated dramatic improvement in AC of whole-body 68Ga-PSMA PET images in the image domain.

articleTitle: Characterization of TlBr Strip Detectors with Waveform Readouts
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) is used to make a variety of clinical diagnoses. Recently there is an increased interest in SPECT systems with improved energy resolution to distinguish between multiple isotopes in alpha-emitting radio-nuclide therapy. Semiconductor detectors are ideal for this task as direct conversion of photon energy yields improved signal statistics. Both strip and pixel configurations can be optimized to meet spatial resolution requirements. Thallium bromide (TlBr) crystals have become of interest due to their high stopping power, large band-gap and ease of crystal purification. Since transport properties and stability has been improved it is timely to develop a complete understanding of TlBr and its best detector configurations. We have developed a time-dependent forward model for double-sided strip detectors. By sampling signal waveforms we have a tool for finding interaction depth and sub-pixel spatial resolution. Our work concludes by comparing simulation results to a TlBr 8x8 strip array developed by RMD. Our results show it may be possible to use "hit" strip waveforms to determine interaction depth. The waveform from the neighbor strips can contribute to sub-strip-pitch spatial resolution.

articleTitle: Simulation of Clock Sequencing Module of High Precision Time Digital Converter for Brain PET
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: High-resolution Time Digital Converter (TDC), a time measurement tool for digitizing time periods to picosecond precision. At present, it is widely used in the frontiers of scientific research fields such as satellite navigation, radar positioning, medical imaging, and high energy physics. Moore's law indicates the rapid progress and development of semiconductor technology. The analogue method has gradually withdrawn from the historical stage, and the digital method based on FPGA (Field program able array) has become the mainstream direction of high-resolution time measurement technology research due to its high flexibility, low cost and short development cycle. In this work, by improving a new phase shift clock sequencing scheme of NUMP (nonuniform multiphase) TDC, a clock sequencing scheme based on FPGA hardline logic resources is designed and verified by simulation. Through simulation analysis, it is found that the hardware sequencing scheme can significantly reduce the time of clock sequencing. To advance the study of high-precision temporal measurement of brain PET.

articleTitle: Application of High Density Digitizer System-on-Chip (HDSoC) Prototype for Acquiring Fast Silicon Photomultiplier Signals
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We present preliminary results on the acquisition of fast silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) signals using HDSoC Version 1, capable of 1-2 giga samples per second (GSa/s) waveform sampling with 32 input channels. Each channel of the HDSoC prototype is aimed at digitizing fast signals from high-channel density SiPM arrays. In this paper, we discuss the estimation of energy (using the digitized signals) corresponding to the SiPM dark counts. The timing uncertainty between the input channels of the digitizer is also discussed.

articleTitle: Single-Modality Supervised Joint PET-MR Image Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We present a new approach for deep learned joint PET-MR image reconstruction. The proposed network is inspired by conventional synergistic methods using a joint regulariser. The maximum a posteriori expectation-maximization algorithm for PET and the Landweber algorithm for MR are unrolled and interconnected through a deep learned joint regularisation step. The parameters of the joint U-Net regulariser and the respective regularisation strengths are learned and shared across all the iterations. Along with introducing this framework, we propose an investigation of the impact of the loss function selection on network performance. We explored how the network performs when trained with a single or a multi-modality loss. Finally, we explored under which settings a joint reconstruction was beneficial for MR reconstruction by using various undersampling factors. The results obtained on 2D simulated data show that the joint networks outperform conventional non-deep learned reconstruction methods, both synergistic and independent. For PET, the network trained with only a PET loss achieves a better global reconstruction accuracy than the version trained with a weighted sum of PET and MR loss terms. More importantly, the former further improves the reconstruction of PET-specific features where deep learned MR-guided methods show their limit. Therefore, using a single-modality loss to supervise the training while still reconstructing the two modalities in parallel leads to better reconstructions and improved modality-unique structure recovery. For MR, while the same effect is observed, the gain from joint reconstruction only occurs in the presence of highly undersampled data.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Non-quadratic Model-based Reconstruction Method for Geometrical Distortion Correction in MR Imaging using Pari Head QC Phantom
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: A major issue when using MR images in precision radiotherapy planning is the geometrical distortion. The magnetic susceptibilities are the primary cause of the geometrical distortion in MR images which could be up to 4 mm across air cavities and body tissue boundaries. The conventional distortion correction approach is not able to completely eliminate the effect of the geometrical distortions. To address this issue, a model-based reconstruction is proposed which benefits from two regularization terms. A regularization term is employed for the correction in the field-map and the other one in the image domain. Regarding the edge smoothing effect of the quadratic functions, non-quadratic penalty functions are proposed for the model-based image reconstruction. In this framework, optimization of the parameters for non-quadratic regularization is highly challenging. In this light, we proposed an approximation approach to select optimized parameters for the model-based reconstitution method. An advantage of the proposed method is that it does not require prior knowledge regarding the ground truth data. To validate the proposed method, BrainWeb phantom was employed for the simulation study. The effectiveness of the proposed approach was further demonstrated experimentally using the Pari head QC phantom customized by SpinTecx-LLC. This phantom would simulate magnetic susceptibility effects in the image due to the presence of air cavities. The simulation study showed a good agreement between the results of the proposed method and the ground truth data. The phantom study further demonstrated the superiority of the proposed method over the conventional approach, wherein the maximum relative intensity difference with respect to the uncorrected image was 10.0% and 2.5% for the proposed approach and the conventional method, respectively. The signal recovery was remarkable for the edges in the non-homogenous regions.

articleTitle: Effects of Different Spectroscopic Filtering Techniques on the Noise Produced by Charge-Sensitive Pre-amplifiers with Feedback Resistors Characterized by High Distributed Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Integrated polysilicon resistors are characterized by a distributed capacitance to bulk which makes them deviate from their ideal theoretical model, especially at high frequency. This difference manifests itself both in terms of impedance and generated noise. Specifically, when using these resistors as feedback discharge devices of charge-sensitive pre-amplifiers, this capacitive coupling turns the thermal white current noise into a non-white one. This noise can be well represented by the sum of two non-correlated components: the first is a white one and the second has a power spectral density proportional to the square root of the frequency. In previous works closed-form calculations have been presented which exhaustively describe impedance and noise power spectrum of such devices. In this work the effects of different types of signal shaping on the contribution to the ENC value of such non-white noise are described. The study includes the most common spectroscopy shaping filters: CR-RC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, quasi-Gaussian and trapezoidal ones and has never been discussed in literature before. All the presented calculations are expressed completely in closed form and without approximation.

articleTitle: Design of Modular Readout Electronics for Cadmium Zinc Telluride (CZT) PET Imaging of the Plants Rhizosphere
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: To study and quantify the dynamic behavior of a plant’s soil-root interface (rhizosphere), we are developing a hybrid positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) system to obtain in situ 3D images to help in modeling the Earth System Model (ESM) in a precise manner. ESM integrates the relevant aspects of the earth system to study the state of climate under various of conditions. The proposed system aims to understand the complex bi-directional flow of carbon in the rhizosphere by quantitatively measuring <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup>C concentration. The rhizosphere imaging requires the creation of a PET system with high sensitivity and excellent spatial resolution; a dual panel geometry of cadmium zinc telluride (CZT) detectors with fine electrodes is being refined and scaled to a 4-panel system to answer the demands. This work focuses on the development, evaluation, and integration of the critical intermediate board (IB) needed to support approximately 5 thousand channels in the CZT PET system and provide modularity to the system. A Rigid-Flex PCB approach is adopted to design the IB. The rigid region will provide firm mechanical support for direct placement of the necessary electronic components and connectors, and the flex region will help to align the subsequent readout boards at the backend of the IB while maintaining the dense packing fraction at front-end where the CZT crystals are connected. Three CZT module (each module comprising of 2-crystals of 39x39 x5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> sandwiched in anode-cathode-cathode-anode configuration) along with 1-mm thick mechanical support on either side of modules will be directly attached to two IBs which forms one tray to modularize the entire system. This modularized design will help to assemble and dissemble the system in an efficient way and minimize the chance of damaging the crystal assemblies. This new IB design will address the troubleshooting/repairing experience and modularity issues that were taking significant amount of time and energy.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Simulation of a Sample Pixelated Detector Aimed at use in Mammography Application in Synchrotron Medical Beamline
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Mammography using the hard X-ray emitted from a synchrotron exploits the monochromatic coherence radiation which can offer better contrast and spatial resolution of the image. In order to enjoy this property, a correlated detector assembly is required. The hybrid pixel semiconductor was proven to be a very powerful tool for medical imaging applications in which a high spatial resolution is demanding. In this paper, considering the importance of simulation in the prefabrication phase of a detector, after evaluating the desirable characteristics of a detector in the application of mammography, a sample detector was proposed and finally its usability in the application of mammography was investigated using simulation. To propose a desirable detector, a hybrid assembly of a GaAs pixel detector with different thicknesses of GaAs substrate and different pixel size was evaluated. Then, the spatial resolution of the proposed detector was characterized by finding the energy deposition of the incident radiation in the detector by Geant4. After that, COMSOL software was used to transport the created charges. The modulation transfer function (MTF) of the detector, which is an important factor to characterize the spatial resolution of an imaging system, was obtained and compared to the experimental and ideal MTFs. The spatial resolution at 30%MTF and 70%MTF for proposed detector with 500µm thickness and 55µm pixel size were obtained equal to 12.8 lp/mm and 7.5 lp/mm, respectively. Also we found that the minimum threshold of visibility, corresponding to 10% MTF, of such detector is 15.80lp/mm, which is an acceptable resolution for detection of mammographic micro-calcifications with dimensions on the order of 500μm. With this resolution we will be able to detect the fine details as small as 63µm. The proposed detector shows high spatial resolution which is suitable for detection of usual small lesions found in mammograms.

articleTitle: A Novel Self-learning Approach based on Object Completion Concept: Evaluated for Lesion Segmentation from MR Images
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Development of a robust and dependable segmentation model requires effective extraction of the underlying pattern/features from the input data. To discriminate the target signal/structure from the background, comprehensive feature maps should be created/extracted which requires a large training dataset. This issue is very critical when the size of the training dataset is sub-optimal. Data-augmentation could partly address this issue, however contrastive- and self-learning techniques have shown promising performance in this regard. This work set out to introduce a novel self-learning framework based on the concept of object completion for the task of segmentation. The proposed object completion and the self-learning framework is guided by entropy image to effectively learn the underlying structures of the input data. Patches of voxels with larger sizes were extracted from the areas bearing a relatively low amount of information (based on the cross-entropy of the input data), while smaller patches of voxel were selected from areas containing a larger amount of information. The performance of the proposed self-learning approach was compared with a conventional data-augmentation technique. Brain lesion segmentation from MR images using the BraTS 2020 was selected to compare the different training frameworks. Evaluation of the segmentation models (training frameworks) on the BraTS dataset demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed self-learning approach with a Dice score of 0.899±0.042, while the original model with no data augmentation (and self-learning) led to a Dice score of 0.860±0.058. After applying a conventional data-augmentation technique, the performance of the model improved to a Dice score of 0.870±0.046. The proposed self-learning approach exhibited superior results compared to the conventional data-augmentation technique. A combination of the proposed self-learning with data-augmentation would lead to improved performance of the segmentation models (as well as reducing the number of outliers in the outcomes).

articleTitle: Improving Sensitivity of Silicon Detectors for X-Ray Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Silicon X-ray detectors, including both silicon drift detectors and SiPIN detectors, are commonly used in X-ray spectroscopy, offering energy resolution near the Fano limit and operation at very high count rates. With vacuum encapsulation and thermoelectric cooling, they are inexpensive and suitable for laboratory and field applications. Though widely used, there are measurements limited by detector sensitivity. Amptek is pursuing three approaches to improve sensitivity.First, most SDDs and SiPINs for X-ray spectroscopy are encapsulated with beryllium windows. Amptek has developed boron carbide-based X-ray windows to deliver better intrinsic efficiency for XRF below 1.5 keV. Second, Amptek has developed larger area detectors, up to 160 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. These offer a large geometric factor and thus high sensitivity in low flux applications. Third, standard silicon X-ray detectors are ≤0.5 mm thick, limiting their intrinsic efficiency over 15 keV, a range including the characteristic X-ray lines of many elements of practical interest. Alternate materials, such as CdTe or HPGe have significant drawbacks. Amptek has developed 1 mm thick SDDs which offer good efficiency above 15 keV with no performance compromise at low energy. The design, performance, and application of detectors using these approaches are presented.

articleTitle: Joint Region of Interest Detection and Bone Age Estimation from Radiograph of the Hand
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Skeletal bone age assessment is a conventional clinical method used to determine adolescent maturity in orthodontics, kinematics, pediatrics, forensic science, and other professions. Bone age is typically determined using the Greulich and Pyle (GP) or Tanner Whitehouse (TW2 or TW3) procedures from radio-graphs of the hand. Because GP and TW methods are subjective and rely on the practitioner's skill, they demand long analysis time, as well as experienced staff. This indicates the necessity for a fully automated approach to determine bone age. In this study, we proposed a robust model to jointly detect wrist area and estimate the bone age from radiograph data. To this end, we initially examined several state-of-the-art Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) models to specify bone age. Then, we proposed the hybrid model, involving two stages. In the first stage, the object detection module selects the key regions of input image to aid the bone age estimation. In the second stage, an attention mechanism based on Residual Neural Networks (ResNet) was included to increase the accuracy of bone age estimation within the classification phase. The mean absolute error for the hybrid model was 0.75 years compared to 1.03, 1.23, 1.08 years obtained from Resnet 18, Resnet 50, and Mobilenet, respectively. The proposed model for joint detection of wrist area and estimation of bone age exhibited superior performance over the conventional networks. This model could be used a decision support tool to reduce the workload/processing time in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Development of 3D Image Reconstruction Method for Beam Online PET Using Irradiation Log Data
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In radiation therapy, confirming that the dose distribution has been formed as planned is necessary. The proton dose distribution cannot be measured since it forms the Bragg peak and stops inside the body. The beam online positron emission tomography (PET) onboard the proton therapy device is used to measure the deposited dose distribution by the proton beam. In this study, it is described that the 3D image reconstruction method from an opposed detector data of OnlinePET using the irradiated log data as time-of-flight (TOF) information. This method was confirmed by Monte Carlo simulation using Geant4. In the image obtained by projecting the 3D reconstructed image, it is possible to discriminate between the irradiated and non-irradiated areas. This study demonstrated the possibility of estimating dose distribution from 3D images reconstructed by OnlinePET data.

articleTitle: A New Demonstrator of Multi-element Germanium Detector With an Optimized Front-end Electronics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This paper reports on a new demonstrator of multi-element germanium detector for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS) applications, with an optimized front-end electronics. The new front-end board can be easily scalable to a large number of channels and has been built in ceramics material for a better vacuum compatibility and temperature homogeneity in germanium crystal. The demonstrator performance has been simulated with a complete simulation chain based on Allpix Square framework and SolidStateDetector software. First simulation and experimental results of the new demonstrator are reported.

articleTitle: Construction and Testing of Novel Designs of Resistive Plate Chambers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) continue to be one of the crucial components of the muon systems in current and future collider experiments, as well as the (semi-)digital hadron calorimeter developed by the CALICE Collaboration. A number of challenges are associated with RPC technology, including issues like loss of particle detection efficiency under high particle flux conditions and limitations associated with conventional RPC gases. To provide solutions to these problems, we have developed new RPC designs with: low resistivity glasses; a single resistive plate; a single resistive plate and a special anode plate coated with a material with high secondary electron emission efficiency. We have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of several designs and are currently in the process of testing the remaining ones to provide supporting evidence. Particularly, the newly developed functional RPCs are investigated in detail to assess the range of possible future implementations. This report focuses on outlining the assembly process for different RPC designs and presenting their performance results from both laboratory tests and beam tests. Additionally, we discuss our forthcoming testing strategies, encompassing extended performance assessments for the recently developed RPCs, investigations into chambers with minimal gas flow, and explorations into the viability of larger chambers.

articleTitle: A Next Generation Preclinical PET/EPRI: a PET Subsystem Prototype
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Previously we reported a PET detector design aiming for a preclinical PET/EPRI hybrid imaging system for studying tumor hypoxia, capable of sub-millimeter spatial resolution and a 100 mm long axial field-of-view. Based on promising results obtained with the exploratory design, in this work we develop a prototype system consisting of four detector modules in a cylindrical supporting frame that has a 115 mm outer diameter. Each of the detector module contains 8 units, each of which in turn is made of a 12x12 array of 1x1x10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> LYSO crystals coupled to a 4x4 Hamamatsu MPPC array (14161-3050HS-04). A highly multiplexing readout employing resistor networks and striplines implemented on a 185 mm x 30 mm printed circuit board is used to produce 6 outputs for the entire detector module. The output signals are recorded by using CAEN DT5742 digitizers and processed off-line. We present the preliminary results obtained with the proto-type PET system, and discuss the prospect of a full detector system.

articleTitle: Timestamp and Amplitude Measurement Solution for Radiation Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Timing has seen an important growth in modern applications like nuclear measurements, digital imaging for SPECT, photon counting, and energy discriminating detectors, just to cite the most commons. In this seance, high-performance Time–to–Digital Converters (TDCs) play a very important role. However, in many applications is quite important acquiring not only the timestamp relative to the arrival time of particles over a specific detector but also the energy itself, that can bring trace as different amplitude levels on the output analog signal. In this paper, we try to find an easy solution to measure the amplitude of the input signal pulses using a multi-channel mixed-signal system composed by a quite fast analog front-end peak detector in a super diode configuration, design with its own Printed-Circuits-Board (PCB), followed by an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) interfaced by a Serial-Peripheral-Interface (SPI) to an FPGA. Moreover, the FPGA hosts a high-performance TDC that is in charge to extract the timestamp to concatenate at the amplitude information. We will use an approach based on Field-Programmable-Gate-Array (FPGA), that is economically more compatible with the scale of the research environment. This choice allows fast time-to-market, fast-prototyping and low non-recursive engineering cost. The PCB will be subsequently connected through a FPGA Mezzanine Card (FMC) connector to the Diligent Nexys Video board in which is host the Artix 200T FPGA. The channel resolution (LSB) of the TDC is 36.6 fs, the number of bit of the ADC is 10, the LSB is FSR(5 V)/2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> = 4.88 mV and the acquisition rate for each channel is 3 M sps.

articleTitle: Performance and Inter-Comparison of Novel 4π-Optimized Compton Imagers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Compton imagers determine the location of a gamma-emitting radioactive source by tracking the interactions of a gamma ray within a position-sensitive spectroscopic gamma detector. The Compton imaging technology is naturally capable of delineating multiple and extended sources as well as localizing point sources. With their graphic output of source location probability contours overlaid on a photograph, Compton imagers are finding application in astronomy, medical imaging, environmental remediation, nuclear nonproliferation and national security. Over the past several years this group has been developing the Silicon photomultiplier-based Compton Telescope for Safety and Security (SCoTSS) imager using a traditional two-plane design with a forward "scatter" plane and a rear "absorber’ plane [1]. At the 2019 IEEE NSS MIC conference we described adapted SCoTSS designs optimized for 4π imaging including cubic, spherical and cruciform geometries and discussed their performance determined from GEANT4 simulations [2]. In this submission we present the results of studies performed on the realized instruments in a laboratory setting, quantifying and comparing their point source response and their imaging uniformity over large fractions the 4π incident angle space. These results, using real data, permit verification of the performance expectations for the various design principles of the detectors.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Motion Correction for Cardiac PET Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Cardiac imaging in PET is susceptible to image degradation from multiple types of motion: myocardial motion due to the cardiac cycle, respiratory motion (which can vary greatly over the course of a scan), and bulk body movements. A comprehensive approach to cardiac motion correction has been developed which addresses each of these types of motion. First, the effect of respiratory motion and bulk body movements on the myocardium is modelled as rigid translation motion; these translations are estimated in image space from short-duration (0.5 s) frames reconstructed over the full duration of the scan. This accounts for variation in respiratory motion because no periodicity is assumed. Next, an ECG signal is used for phase-based gating of the myocardial cycle. The cardiac gated reconstructions incorporate event-by-event motion correction from the estimated translations. The resulting cardiac gated series presents the heart at a fixed position, with only cardiac motion between gates. Finally, the cardiac gated images are combined into a single volume via non-rigid registration using the Q.Freeze2 package from GE HealthCare. This approach provides a single fully motion-corrected, quantitative image of the myocardium that utilizes all counts. Results from this approach are shown on NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> data with the reconstructions showing improved contrast and signal-to-noise.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Stationary Tomographic MBI System Including Non-Local Means Filtering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: A novel stationary tomographic Molecular Breast Imaging (MBI) system is currently under development, with the aim of obtaining high image-quality with low dose and short scanning time. The system is based on dual opposing CZT detector arrays and multi-pinhole collimators. We have recently modified the iterative image reconstruction procedure by incorporating a novel relaxation scheme, in order to make the image contrast and noise properties more uniform throughout the field-of-view. In addition, we have introduced a post-reconstruction image denoising step based on the non-local means (NLM) filter. In view of the significant effect that these steps had on the image quality, we performed a new system parameter optimization. The parameters investigated were pinhole size, opening angle and separation, as well as the number of reconstruction iterations and the degree-of-smoothing parameter of the NLM filter. The optimization was performed based on simulated data, by maximizing the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the images. We found that the optimal system parameters were not so different with the new data processing steps as compared to previous results, while the CNR was improved by a factor > 3.

Index Terms: Center Of The Field Of View

articleTitle: Compact DSP-based Time-to-Digital Converter IP-Core for Xilinx 7-Series
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this contribution, we present the implementation of a compact, multi-channel, and high-resolution Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) IP-Core implemented using the Digital Signal Processor (DSP) blocks present in the 28-nm Xilinx 7-Series Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). The very high-resolution is obtained using the classical tapped delay-line approach where the delay-line is implemented thanks to the adder chain of the DSP blocks, i.e. the DSP48E1 primitive. Exploiting this type of resource, instead of the classical CARRY primitive, makes possible to build a more compact structure also leading to relax the hardware utilization. Indeed, the sampling of the tapped delay-line is made by the flip-flops (FFs) integrated in the DSP itself, thus not requiring to use the FFs present in the FPGA fabric as in the CARRY approach.This device is also tunable, thanks to the possibility of setting the resolution (LSB), some picoseconds, and Full-Scale Range (FSR), up to some days, from the user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) of the IP-Core. Last but not least, the TDC is also characterized by a maximum measurement rate in the order of hundreds of Msps per channel, thus satisfying the high count-rate capability required by state-of-the-art detectors. To obtain such an high-resolution over a wide FSR, the measurement is performed according to the Nutt-Interpolation technique, in which the timestamp of each channel is made by a coarse counter part and by a fine part performed by the DSP. From an experimental point of view, the TDC, with a few tens of channels, has been implemented and fully tested on an Artix-7 FPGA (xc7a100tftg256-2).

articleTitle: Characterization of First Prototypes Fabricated in 65nm CMOS Technology for the ALICE Inner Tracking System Upgrade
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: For the next detector upgrade, the ALICE experiment carries out an R&D programme with the purpose of minimizing the material budget by removing the passive components and keeping just the silicon layer. The goal is to build a new vertex tracker, the Inner Tracking System 3, based on curved, wafer-scale, ultra-thin Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors (MAPS) arranged in truly cylindrical layers. This will not only allow to achieve a material budget of about 0.05% of a radiation length X0, but also to place the innermost layer at a radial distance of only 18 mm from the interaction point. The technology proposed for this upgrade is the 65 nm CMOS imaging process by TowerJazz Panasonic Semiconductor Company which allows the production of wafer-scale pixel sensors on 300 mm wafers using stitching. After thinning to 50 μm or below each sensor can be bent to a radius as small as 18mm to form a half of the cylindrical detection layer. Therefore, six stitched sensors are sufficient to construct three new innermost layers made essentially of only thin silicon. A first prototyping run in this technology, which was carried out together with the CERN EP R&D programme, included a number of pixel test structures to evaluate the charged particle detection performance of the 65 nm technology as well as its radiation hardness. In particular, a set of 4×4 pixel matrices with parallel, analog readout in various geometries are used to map the parameter space. Two other sets of chips feature larger matrices of 64×32 pixels with rolling shutter analog readout, and 32×32 pixel matrices with digital in-pixel discrimination and digital readout. This contribution will cover the results of performance measurements on the mentioned prototype chips, obtained both in the laboratory and with particle beams. Finally, the outlook for the next submissions towards the final large-scale sensor will be given.

articleTitle: Low Dose Myocardial Perfusion SPECT Denoising Using an Attention-Based Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Deep learning-based denoising is promising for low dose (LD) myocardial perfusion (MP) SPECT. However, conventional convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods used fixed-sized convolutional kernels to convolute one region within the receptive field at a time, which would be ineffective for learning the feature dependencies across large regions. Attention scheme is able to leverage voxels with stronger correlations beyond the kernel receptive field. In this study, we propose a 3D attention-based conditional generative adversarial network (AttcGAN) for denoising LD MP-SPECT images on both projection- and reconstruction-domain. Forty-six patients underwent ~1184 MBq <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">99m</sup>Tc-sestamibi stress SPECT/CT scan were retrospectively recruited. Sixty projections were acquired from right anterior oblique to left posterior oblique positions and the acquisition time for each projection was 10 s for the full dose (FD) mode. LD MP-SPECT images (1/10 to 7/10 of FD) were generated from the FD list mode data. cGAN and AttcGAN were implemented using Tensorflow with the Adam optimizer running up to 200 epochs. FD and LD MP-SPECT pairs of 30 patients were used for training the cGAN and AttcGAN separately for each dose level, while 6, and 10 patients were applied for validation and testing. Normalized mean square error (NMSE), normalized standard deviation (NSD), and perfusion defect size (PDS) were analyzed. The results indicate that denoising on the projection-domain outperforms reconstruction-domain for both networks, and the AttcGAN is superior to cGAN on both projection- and reconstruction-domain on all dose levels. We conclude that AttcGAN denoising on projection-domain can further improve the denoising performance for LD MP-SPECT with better defect quantification accuracy.

articleTitle: Deep Vision Transformers for Prognostic Modeling in COVID-19 Patients using Large Multi-Institutional Chest CT Dataset
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The importance of prognosis is the assessment of the disease progression, providing more effective management, decreasing mortality, and lowering the time of hospital stay. In convolutional neural network (CNN)-based algorithms, explicit long-range and global relation modeling is a major challenge because of the locality of convolution operations. These challenges result in weak performance because of large inter/intra-patient variabilities, specifically in COVID-19 patients. Transformers successfully used in natural language processing (NLP) tasks could potentially address the limitation of CNN-based algorithms. In the current study, we evaluated deep transformers-based algorithms’ performances in the prognostication of COVID-19 patients. Patient data from 19 centers were enrolled in this study. After inclusion and exclusion criteria, 2339 patients remained (1278 alive and 1061 deceased). We implemented a pure Transformer that consists Swin Transformer block. Images split into non-overlap patches (4 by 4) are used as tokens by the patch partitioner, followed by a linear embedding layer. These tokens pass through the patch merging layer and the Swin transformer block (feature representation learning). In addition, we implemented CNN-based algorithms, including ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ResNet-101, and DensNet, for comparison. Data were split into train/validation (70%) and test sets (30%), and all evaluations were performed on test sets. The accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were reported for the test sets (unseen during training). Regarding AUCs, 0.66, 0.75, 0.72, 0.77, and 0.81 were achieved by ResNet-18, Resnet-50, Resnet-101, DensNet, and Transformers.Considering all parameters Transformer significantly (p-value <0.05) outperformed all CNN-based models with Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity, and AUC of 0.75, 0.78, 0.71, and 0.81, respectively.

articleTitle: First-principle SiPM Characterization to Enable Radiation Detection in Harsh Environments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This paper reports the experimental comparison of two silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs): the MicroFJ-30035 by ONSemi and the ASD-NUV3S-P by AdvanSiD, in terms of gain, dark count rate, and crosstalk probability. SiPMs are solid state photon detectors that enable high sensitivity light readout. They have low-voltage power requirements, small form factor, and are durable. For these reasons, they are being considered as replacements for vacuum photomultiplier tubes in some applications. However, their performance relies on several parameters, which need to be carefully characterized to enable their high-fidelity simulation and SiPM-based design of devices capable to operate in harsh environments. The parameters tend to vary between manufacturers and processing technologies. In this work, we have compared the MicroFJ and ASD SiPMs in terms of gain, dark count rate, and crosstalk probability. We found that the dark count rate of the MicroFJ was 16% higher than the ASD. Also, the gain of the MicroFJ is 3.5 times higher than the ASD. Finally, the crosstalk probability of the ASD 1.96 times higher than the MicroFJ. Our findings are in good agreement with manufacturer reported values.

articleTitle: Resolution Recovery by PSF Deconvolution on List Mode MLEM Reconstruction for Dynamic Cardiac SPECT System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This work presents improvement in imaging resolution by implementing spatial variant point spread function (SV-PSF) with list mode MLEM reconstruction for the DC-SPECT system being developed at MGH, Harvard. Results show that with PSF modeling applied, quality of the reconstructed image is improved, and DC-SPECT system can achieve a 4.5 mm central spatial resolution with average 795 counts/(s*Mbq).
