Finally, the SR model performance is quantitatively evaluated by peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) using the test patient images. Cubic spline interpolation and a generative adversarial network (GAN) with cycle consistency ("GAN-CIRCLE") are used for comparison. TTSR can restore more details in SRCT images than interpolation and GAN-CIRCLE. The quantitative results of PSNR and SSIM also show that TTSR can achieve the best performance. We finally show that TTSR using only 1/4 of all projection data can outperform LDCT with advanced denoising using all projection data. This development paves a way for deep learning-based SR for CT with lessened requirement on the number of detectors and much reduced computation time.

articleTitle: SLAC Femtosecond Laser Timing Synchronization System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: SLAC femtosecond laser timing synchronization system is an FPGA based real time feedback control system that synchronizes laser oscillator to RF reference signal on femtosecond timing scale. The system was first installed on SLAC mega-electron-volt (MeV) ultrafast electron diffraction (UED) instrument in 2019 and has achieved 10 femtosecond laser-RF timing jitter on the UED laser oscillator. Since then, the system has been installed in a few other SLAC laser facilities, such as the LCLS (Linac Coherent Light Source) - II injector laser, LCLS-II pump-probe lasers, etc. These lasers have different tuning ranges from a few Hz per volt to a few hundred Hz per volt and tuning bandwidth from a few kHz to hundreds kHz. We have recently upgraded the firmware design to enable a wider operating range so that the system can be used on various SLAC lasers with different tuning parameters. This presentation describes the system algorithm, its FPGA implementation and test results from various lasers.

articleTitle: An Experimental Device to Investigate Columnar Recombination Models
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss electron-ion recombination processes in gaseous argon with the aim to improve fission chambers models. Boag-Chabod’s model of columnar recombination is presented and its parameters detailed. The dimensioning of an experimental device to investigate this model is proposed. The specifications and the simulation of the device are presented. We conclude on the expected results and prospects of this study.

articleTitle: Non-quadratic Regularization Parameters Selection for Model-based Geometrical Distortion Correction of MRI images
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Nowadays, MRI has received lots of attention as the only method of imaging in radiation therapy. However, MR images suffer from distortions induced by magnetic susceptibility effects that can be up to 2-4 mm at air-tissue interfaces, which is the main concern in precision radiation therapy planning. The conventional method for MR distortion correction is the field-mapping which is not able to completely correct distortions due to residual intensity and geometrical distortions in the field-map. To address this issue, a model-based reconstruction which has two regularization terms, one for image and the other for field-map correction was presented. Due to the edge smoothing effect of the quadratic penalty function, non-quadratic penalties were proposed and investigated for the model-based MR image reconstruction. In this regard, selecting proper regularization parameters for non-quadratic regularization is challenging due to the lack of prior knowledge about the ground truth image. This work set out to propose an approximation method for selecting optimized parameters for image and field-map regularization in the model-based reconstruction. To validate the proposed method, BrainWeb phantom simulation data was used. When the Huber and Lange1 penalty functions were employed, the estimated regularization parameters by the proposed method led to the minimum root mean square error (RMSE) and maximum peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) for the reconstructed image versus the ground truth data. The results demonstrated a good agreement between the results obtained from the proposed method and the ground truth data. The simulation study demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method in reducing the MR image distortion for the purpose of precision radiation therapy planning.

articleTitle: A Dual-head Prompt Gamma Imaging System for Online Monitoring in Proton Therapy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Proton therapy is one of the most advanced radiotherapy technologies. However, due to range uncertainty, real-time monitoring of proton dose deposition is of great importance in proton therapy.A dual-head prompt gamma imaging system has been proposed in previous work. The system design provides high spatial resolution and ensures enough detection efficiency for high signal-to-noise imaging during pencil beam scanning. In this work, the dual-head imaging system is assembled and calibrated. Detectability of range shift and range deviation accuracy are evaluated under 60 and 100 MeV proton beam. Detection efficiency (at the center of the FOV) and spatial resolution of the dual-head system are given by point source experiment.Range shift of 1 mm is able to be distinguished by the vertical detector by locating the most distal edge position (MDEP) of prompt gamma profile. Proton range deviation and range deviation accuracy of the vertical detector are both less than 1 mm at typical count level of a single spot in pencil beam scanning. Detection efficiency of the dual-head imaging system is 0.62% (FOV center) and ≤3 mm spatial resolution is achieved in the whole FOV.The dual-head prompt gamma imaging system shows excellent performance in detection efficiency and spatial resolution. Proton range shift detectability of the system is preliminarily verified. The system should be tested under clinical proton beam setup in future work.

articleTitle: Minimizing Power Consumption for Time-of-Flight PET SiPM Readout
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Good energy and timing resolutions are critical parameters for new generations of PET detectors. In particular, implementing detectors with minimum electronics, potentially only passive components, is desired. This will improve the cost but, more importantly, the power consumption of the final scanner, which will further reduce requirements for cooling and space. In this work, we benchmark four circuit configurations with low power consumption. The tests were carried out using 3x3x5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> LYSO:Ce:Ca crystals and FBK NUV SiPM. The best scenarios provide a combination of 7% energy resolution and 91 ps CTR with the cost of 300 mW power consumption per detector, with two channels, and 115.1 ps and 12% energy resolution for a circuit without active components and a virtual zero power consumption, with one channel. We will further develop these solutions into system-level arrays with deployment potential.

articleTitle: Prediction Pathological Structure of Computed Tomographic Colonography Polyps via Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Computed tomographic colonography (CTC) has shown to be an effective means of detecting the precursor polyps leading to colorectal cancer (CRC). Accurately diagnosing these polyps can assist the overall treatment plan and follow-up examination determination to prevent CRC. In this work, we examine a machine learning approach to predicting the three main pathological structure type of polyps, comparing hyperplastic and serrated adenomas (HS), tubular adenomas (TA), and advanced neoplasms (AN). We find that imaging textures can differentiate any two pathological groups with AUC scores ranging from 0.624-0.749 for polyps less than 10mm in size and 0.731-0.887 for polyps greater than 10mm. Classification of all three pathology groups simultaneously shows a sensitivity of 61.6% for identifying the highest risk group of advanced neoplasms.

articleTitle: Development of a Pixelated BaF2 Test Bed for Timing Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Prototype pixelated BaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> detectors for timing applications have been assembled using state-of-the-art commercial off-the-shelf components. 64 square rods of pure BaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (4.6 mm × 4.6 mm × 30 mm) are air-coupled in an 8 × 8 array to a Photonis XP85112 Planacon multianode microchannel plate photomultiplier tube; shortpass optical transmission interference filters may be inserted between the crystal array and photodetector to suppress the slow, self-trapped exciton luminescence. Three filter variants with different long wavelength cutoffs were tested experimentally, and the performance of each filter is assessed. The results of these and upcoming detector characterization exeriments will ascertain how well new technologies can leverage the unique timing properties of BaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in a practical system, and provide quantitative guidance for effective continued development.

articleTitle: Impact of X-ray Spectra Modeling on Gain and Noise Determination in High-dynamic Range Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The accuracy in the determination of gain and noise from X-ray spectra becomes critical when the data binning is larger with respect to noise, situation often encountered in high-dynamic range systems. In such conditions, the spectral components in the peak shape of the X-ray line to be fitted, if not correctly modelled, cause significant distortions in the fit results.We tested fitting models with increasing levels of accuracy, in order to study the impact on gain and noise determination from X-ray spectra. The main fitting options (e.g. low-energy shoulder related to charge collection inefficiency, bremsstrahlung, beam filtration, bin integration) have been tested on experimental spectra acquired by DEPFET pixels at low bin resolution. A dedicated analysis has been carried out to compare noise estimation by spectra fitting with and without bin integration on simulated data sets and on experimental data.

articleTitle: Electrical and Optical Characterizations of the BNL Low Gain Avalanche Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Low Gain Avalanche Detectors (LGADs) are promising candidates that have been considered for the future applications of 4D-tracking section, which is an important part of the current upgrades of ATLAS and CMS timing detectors to be used in the future operations of the High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider at CERN. This type of sensor features good radiation hardness and fast timing properties featuring a moderate gain in linear-mode operation, thanks to the special engineering of its internal gain layer. In general, different factors like temperature, bias voltage, radiation type and radiation intensity can affect the gain of the detectors. A complete understanding of these effects requires careful analysis through experiments and simulations to find the best compromise among various aspects and enhance their time resolution in the real harsh environments. This paper describes a summary of the experiments done on the gain suppression mechanism of LGAD devices developed at Brookhaven National Laboratory for charged particles detection. Static electrical characterization of the prototypes will also be reported. A fast pulsed IR laser was used in the lab to investigate how the BNL-Detectors’ gains change depending to the input light intensity and the applied reverse bias voltages. Three different ranges of radiation intensities and bias voltages (low, medium and high) were covered during the measurements and finally, a relationship was observed as expected and the results confirmed the fact that the gain values reduce at the higher input radiation intensity and larger reverse bias voltages, due to space charge effects, i.e. the electric field generated by the mobile charges that are crossing the high field region. In addition, a gain value between 60-70 was calculated at the high range voltages close to the device breakdown voltage (380V).

articleTitle: Tau PET Image Harmonization Using a Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Multi-scanner image harmonization is a major challenge for longitudinal imaging studies that often span several decades and transition from legacy scanners to state-of-the-art alternatives. In this preliminary tau PET imaging study involving 5 human subjects sequentially scanned on a GE Discovery MI PET/CT scanner and a Siemens HR+ scanner, we train and validate a generative adversarial network (GAN) for harmonizing tau PET images between the two scanners. Our network receives as inputs an HR+ image, a high-resolution anatomical MR image, and spatial information. The method was validated on clinical data by comparing the synthetic images generated by the GAN with those generated by a convolutional neural network (CNN) and by deconvolution stabilized by a total variation penalty. Our results show that the GAN outperforms both classical deblurring and the CNN in terms of image quality and quantitation as indicated by the peak signal-to-noise-ratio.

articleTitle: Development of A Multi-layer Silicon Beta-ray Dosemeter for CANDU Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: There is a growing demand for precise dose assessment to the lens of eye from beta radiation at CANDU power plants. We present the design of a silicon-based beta-ray dosemeter to meet such needs. The primary objective of the dosemeter is to measure the in situ beta-ray fluence rate spectrum and monitor the dose rates for eye, skin and whole body in real-time. We aim to accomplish the minimum gamma rejection ratio 1000:1 to avoid the beta dose overestimation. To achieve the objective, the beta radiation dosemeter features a telescopic configuration of a stack of three 40 mm diameter planar Si detectors with different thicknesses that can cover a beta energy range of 70 keV to 3000 keV using the ΔE vs. E method. Customized detector housing and front-end electronics including power and preamp module are developed. A microcontroller (MCU)-based data acquisition (DAQ), control system, firmware and software are currently under development. MCNP simulations were performed to optimize the instrument design. In this paper, we report the hardware architecture, MCNP results and preliminary characterization of a prototype system.

articleTitle: Irradiation Testing of HGCROC3: the Front-End Readout ASIC for the CMS High Granularity Calorimeter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The HGCROC3 is the final version of the front-end ASIC designed to readout the 6 million channels of the future HGCAL detector. Along with cutting-edge specifications in terms of low noise, time measurement precision, and ability to contribute to the Level-1 trigger decision, one of the key requirements for the HGCROC3 is a high radiation tolerance.Several irradiation campaigns have been carried out on HGCROC3 prototypes, with particular emphasis on the Total Integrated Dose (TID) and the Single-Event Effect (SEE) tests. In the context of the TID campaign, results are presented in terms of power consumption, charge and time measurement performance, clocks, and serial links robustness. Although previous versions of the same ASIC architecture show encouraging results in terms of SEE hardness, in this final version of the chip a special care is taken to reach the radiation tolerance requirement for critical blocks such as the digital counters, the clocks and the serializers. The corresponding studies of SEE effects on these components are also reported in this contribution.

articleTitle: Measurement Results for the High Density digitizer System on Chip (HDSoC): A Waveform Digitizer for High Density Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This paper presents measurements of the performance of the first revisions of the HDSoC, a waveform sampling ASIC optimized for high density photo-detectors, such as Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) or MA-PMTs. The first revision of HDSoC is operating at 1 Gigasample/sec waveform sampling with the ability to service 32 channels (the second revision is planned to cover 64 channels). The HDSoC is a System-on-Chip with built-in SiPM biasing, input TIA, with internally controlled digitization via a digital core that allows independent operation of each of the channels permitting low latency and high data rate, as well as multiple acquisition modes including dead timeless operation within a rate limit. In this paper we cover extensive test results and plans for future revisions.

articleTitle: Segmentation Ability of Pulmonary Nodules Using Deep Learning in Dual-Energy Subtraction Images
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In recent years, computer-aided detection (CAD) systems for chest X-ray (CXR) images have been promoted to decrease the number of deaths from lung cancer and to overcome the shortage of radiologists. Dual-energy subtraction (DES) images of pulmonary nodules have been reported to provide higher detection rates than CXR, but DES has the disadvantage of increasing the radiation dose. Therefore, in this study, DES images were obtained using an entrance surface dose half of that used in CXR by incorporating a noise reduction process. The automatic segmentation of pulmonary nodules, one of the important steps of CAD, was performed using deep learning techniques. Segmented images of the pulmonary nodules were created for use with U-net, one of the deep learning techniques, and the detection accuracy of the pulmonary nodules was compared for CXR and DES images. The data for the U-net were prepared from 348 CXR images and from the same number of DES images obtained using artificial nodules placed on a commercially available anthropomorphic lung phantom. Since noise reduction was important for improving pulmonary nodule segmentation in DES images, the DES images were pre-processed with a bilateral filter, a non-local means filter, and an anti-correlated noise reduction (ACNR) algorithm. In the artificial nodule segmentation, the recall and the precision were higher in the DES images with noise reduction processes than in the CXR images. These results suggest the usefulness of CAD in DES images taken at an entrance surface dose of half the CXR dose.

articleTitle: Effects of Data Corrections on Image Quality for a Brain Dedicated PET Insert for MRI
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Creating an organ-dedicated PET system facilitates compact high-sensitivity geometries capable of high spatial resolution with a good image signal-to-noise ratio. The Molecular Imaging Instrumentation Laboratory has dedicated effort to developing an economically friendly brain-dedicated insert intended for simultaneous PET/MR imaging. This first-generation insert has been structurally modified for clinical translation with the near completion of the algorithmic foundation for maximum image quality. This work reports the accuracy and impact of data corrections such as normalization, randoms subtraction, attenuation correction, and scatter correction on a contrast phantom prepared with a signal-to-background ratio of 4:1. The final contrast ratio was calculated to be 2.64 for the largest rod in our phantom. Scatter estimation proved especially difficult given the compact system geometry.

articleTitle: A Novel CT Geometry
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: A conventional state-of-the-art CT detector forms an arc concentric to the x-ray source. For the cone-beam to parallel-beam conversion prior to the reconstruction, both channel- and view-wise rebinning are required, which leads to a compromised spatial resolution and elevated aliasing artifact. We present a novel detector geometry that enables the acquisition of projections with an evenly spaced distance to the isocenter. To ensure that the detector has a uniform cell size, the source-to-detector distance becomes a function of the detector fan-angle. The channel-wise rebinning to form a parallel dataset is therefore eliminated. Extensive computer simulations were used to verify our design. The proposed design offers a 12.6% increase in spatial resolution, resulting from a reduced detector cell size and the removal of the channel-wise interpolation. In addition, aliasing artifact is significantly reduced at locations away from the isocenter. At matched spatial resolution, image noise for the proposed system is 8.8% lower. Further research on this design is warranted to fully explore important systems parameters such as the compactness of the gantry design.

articleTitle: Separation of Overlapped Projection Images in Multi-pinhole SPECT System With a Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We propose an image reconstruction method for the overlapping projection images that occur when using a multi-pinhole single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) system. Generally, data acquisition in SPECT systems is performed with rotating gamma cameras. Therefore, data acquisition is time-consuming and dynamic study of organs is not possible. In addition, a patient must remain in a certain posture during data acquisition, which is a significant burden. On the other hand, system with multi-pinhole collimators from a limited direction range, they enable stationary data acquisition in multi-head SPECT systems and have many advantages such as dynamic data acquisition and reduced patient stress due to shorter data acquisition time. However, one of the disadvantages of this system is its low sensitivity. When the number of pinholes increases to improve the data acquisition angles and sensitivity, the projection images of the pinholes overlap, resulting in artifacts in a reconstructed image. To address this issue, when we avoid the overlap of the projection images, the spatial resolution of the reconstructed image is reduced. In this paper, we propose a method to separate overlapped projection images in a multi-pinhole SPECT system using a neural network. We confirmed that the overlapped projection images can be removed.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial-based Framework for Classification using Imbalance Data: Application to Pneumonia Detection in Chest Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Pneumonia is an infectious lung illness in humans that affects one or both lungs which is caused by the fungus, bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms. Due to the difficulty of identifying this lung illness at early stages, children below the age of five years and aged people are easily affected by this illness. In this light, early diagnosis and treatment of these diseases are critical. Pneumonia detection requires experienced specialists to identify the pneumonia symptoms from chest X-ray radiography, which is time-consuming and costly in clinical practice. Thus, an automated pneumonia classification from X-ray chest data is highly valuable. Despite the extraordinary performance of the deep learning approaches, some of the proposed methods suffer from issue of imbalance data, insufficient number of labeled data for a specific disease type, as well as errors in the labelled data. In this light, we set out to propose a method with the least possible supervising for training with the minimum amount of data¸ to provide a robust solution for the issue of training with imbalance dataset. The proposed framework tends to regenerate/estimate new features (data-augmentation in the feature map) from X-ray images with GAN. Features are produced by a competition between the Generator, Feature Extractor network, and the Discriminator network. The novel Semi-Supervised GAN-Based method to overcome the issue imbalance data was evaluated using an imbalance dataset for pneumonia detection. The results showed that the proposed framework outperforms the baseline Network, that used an end-to-end supervised learning approach, with a 5.3% improvement in classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Digital SiPMs in a 110 nm CMOS Technology with Fast Parallel Counter Architecture
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a digital silicon photomultiplier (dSiPM) in a 110 nm CMOS technology. The detection pulses, generated by an array of single photon avalanche diodes (SPADs), are simultaneously read out in real time by means of a fast parallel counter, which was designed using a purposely developed algorithm. The problem of spurious pulses (glitches), generated during the counting operation, was strongly mitigated by equalizing the internal propagation delays. A balanced symmetric full adder was designed for this purpose. Dedicated circuits devoted to the rejection of individual dark pulses and to the implementation of a signal over threshold (SOT) logic have been included in the structure.

articleTitle: Gamma-ray Spectra from a 3x3 CsPbBr3 Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is a promising semiconductor material for X-and ℽ-ray detection at room temperature due to a wide bandgap of 2.3 eV, high stopping power, and relatively high mobility-lifetime products of electrons and holes, and the capability of growing large crystals. In this paper we report on fabrication and testing of a 3.8 mm thick, 3 × 3 array with 1.25 mm pitch. Raw <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">137</sup>Cs spectra were acquired with applied bias of 400 V, 500 V, and 600 V. Energy resolution of between 2 and 3 % FWHM at 662 keV was obtained from most pixels without any correction at room temperature. After 29 days under continuous bias at 600 V, no polarization effects were observed.

articleTitle: Pulse Shape Discrimination of Shielded and Unshielded 252Cf in Organic Glass Scintillators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Organic scintillators can detect both neutrons and gamma rays, making them a common instrument used in nuclear nonproliferation applications. Pulse shape discrimination (PSD) is a well-established technique used to distinguish different types of radiation detected by organic scintillators. Scientists at Sandia National Laboratories have recently developed an organic glass scintillating material that is capable of PSD. To explore the performance of this material and its potential in nonproliferation fields, experiments using gamma and neutron sources to evaluate PSD capabilities must be conducted. In this work, we present new experimental results of organic glass rectangular scintillators of varying thickness and optical wrapping. We assess the PSD performance as a function of detector thickness and optical reflector type using a figure of merit. The organic glass scintillators with optical reflective wrappings outperform the bare organic glass scintillators.

articleTitle: Hybrid In-Vivo Treatment Verification for Particle Therapy: Multivariate Modelling of Fast Neutron and Prompt Gamma-Ray Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Given its sensitivity to anatomical variations, particle therapy is expected to benefit strongly from reliable on-line treatment verification. Making use of a large fraction of the secondary particles available, hybrid prompt gamma-ray and fast neutron imaging is a promising approach for this purpose. We present a simulation study introducing a novel method for range reconstruction by means of these particles. To this end, the passage of a proton beam through a patient and the detection of secondary particles in a dedicated detector array were simulated by Monte Carlo particle transport calculations. Anatomical variations were mimicked by adding or removing tissue to the patient. The secondary particle production vertices were reconstructed from the events registered by the detector based on scatter kinematics and maximum likelihood expectation maximisation. The vertices were projected onto the beam axis and the most predictive features of the resulting distributions were identified from a standardised feature set by forward feature selection and the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO). A range-shift sensitivity of 1 mm or less was reached at intensities of 1.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> protons per spot with fast neutrons, and at 2.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> protons per spot with prompt gamma-rays. These results demonstrate the potential of particle treatment verification by fast neutrons and prompt gamma-rays and strengthen the potential of this hybrid system for clinical application.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Tumour Delineation on Photon-counting CT Images
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Treatment planning for stereotactic radiosurgery is based on manual delineation of tumour volumes and image registration of the CT and MRI patient scan, which can lead to uncertainties in the clinical workflow. These could be alleviated by implementing deep learning-based tumour contouring and a single modality imaging technique. This study investigates the performance of the deep learning models DeepMedic and nnU-Net for automatic tumour segmentation on two different data sets. In a first experiment, both models are trained on MRI data for vestibular schwannoma segmentation. A second experiment assesses the performance of a 2D nnU-Net model on a glioma data set including MRI and CT data. Additionally, the simulation framework GATE is used to simulate and reconstruct energy-integrating and photon-counting images of a simple brain phantom including a tumour volume. The 2D nnU-Net trained on the glioma CT data is applied to these images.All of the investigated networks achieve a high performance for vestibular schwannoma segmentation on MRI data. However, the performance achieved of the 2D nnU-Net model on the glioma data is low. A possible reason could be the heterogeneity of the data set. Investigation of this is part of ongoing work.The photon-counting image with a 50 keV threshold shows the best contrast to differentiate between tumour and brain tissue for our phantom. However, the 2D nnU-Net is not able to delineate the tumour on any of the reconstructed images which can be explained by the lack of higher-level brain features in the phantom.The results of this work show the need of incorporating a more realistic brain anatomy into the system and improvement of the network training and image reconstruction pipeline.

articleTitle: 3D Event Reconstruction in Radiation Detectors using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Room Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (RTSDs) such as CdZnTe are being widely used in diverse applications, to provide interaction position of γ-rays and excellent energy resolution. These sensors are often pixelated. The full potential of these RTSDs are explored while developing advanced single-polarity charge sensing reconstruction algorithms. Current position and energy reconstruction algorithms rely on physical models. Deep learning (DL) techniques can perform event reconstruction with better energy resolution and improved position information than conventional non-DL methods. Here we present a DL approach based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to identify the 3D interaction position and energy deposition of the γ-rays in a single pixel CdZnTe detector. The network is trained in a supervised fashion with input-output data pairs. The input data to the DL model consists of voltage signals at the electrodes from the superposition of signals generated from each hit of an incident event on the single pixel detector and the output data consists of the 3D position and energy deposited in those hits. The DL model consists of 5 stages of convolutional layers. Every convolutional layer is followed by successive batch normalization and max-pooling layers. These layers extract features from the input data. After the feature extraction, there are 2 stages of fully connected layers. The 3D hit positions and energies deposited by those events are output of this model.

articleTitle: Model-based and Data-driven Calibration of the X-ray CT Image based on Proton Radiographies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In proton beam therapy the semi-empirical calibration of the X-ray CT image introduces inaccuracies into the treatment planning. The promise of proton imaging is to potentially eliminate these inaccuracies by (1) replacing the X-ray CT image with the proton CT image based on tomographic image reconstruction of many proton radiographies or (2) adjusting the semi-empirical calibration of the X-ray CT image based on optimization algorithms for few proton radiographies. Both (1) and (2) are based on the model of the proton radiography (in water equivalent thickness, WET) as a line integral of the proton CT image (in relative stopping power, RSP) along the estimation of the proton trajectory. However, this model (i.e., the forward-projection) is not perfectly consistent to the measurement (i.e., the proton radiography). Depending on the detector configurations, in clinical data these intrinsic inconsistencies can result in the same order of magnitude as the calibration inaccuracies that are intended to be eliminated. The purpose of this work is to overcome the intrinsic limitation of the model-based optimization with a novel data-driven approach relaying on supervised machine learning. The availability of the ground truth CT image in simulations is exploited. Realistic proton radiographies are simulated relying on pre-clinical data. Results demonstrate the potential capability of the data-driven approach. A tuning of the hyperparameters and the number of layers of the convolutional neural network is ongoing. Further investigations involving different data and different detector configurations are foreseen.

articleTitle: Design of a Radiation-Tolerant Bandgap Voltage Reference for HEP applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This work discusses the design of a bandgap voltage reference circuit to be operated in harsh radiation environments. The circuit, designed in a standard 28 nm CMOS technology with a core voltage supply of 0.9 V, exhibits in simulations an average output voltage of about 480 mV with an average temperature coefficient of 22 ppm/°C in the range [-40°C, 60°C]. Some preliminary results of the characterization are also presented.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of Activity, Attenuation and Motion in Respiratory-Gated Time-of-Flight PET
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In PET imaging, the patient’s respiratory motion during the scan is unavoidable and has an important impact on the quality of the reconstructed image, creating motion artifacts which can alter the clinical’s diagnosis. Correcting for these artefacts involves several challenges, in particular the estimation of the respiratory waveform and the design of an efficient motion corrected image reconstruction method. In this study we use a data-driven strategy to estimate the respiratory waveform, and then we developed a joint motion estimation and image reconstruction approach for TOF-PET. This joint approach reconstructs a unique 3D activity image at a "virtual" position and introduces non-smooth regularizations on the non-rigid displacements and the reconstructed activity image. This joint approach is based on the Alternating Directions Method of Multipliers (ADMM) which leads to several optimization sub-problems. These are solved with a Maximum A Posteriori estimation of the activity simultaneously with the estimation of the attenuation factors, and regularized non-parametric registrations to estimate displacements for each gate. We validated the method on experimental list-mode TOF-PET data obtained with the Siemens Biograph mCT PET/CT system and an anthropomorphic thorax phantom which simulates respiratory motion.

articleTitle: A Wireless Probe Based on a Dual-Tier CMOS SPAD Array for Charged Particle Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a novel low-energy particle probe based on single photon avalanche diode (SPAD) detectors. The APIX2LF sensor chip contains a vertically interconnected, dual-tier SPAD array with passive quenching fabricated in a 150 nm CMOS standard technology. A microcontroller interfaces with the SPAD detector and sends pre-processed data to the PC wirelessly. A graphical user interface makes it possible to read and plot data in real-time. The system can be USB or battery powered making the probe easy to use in many different environments.

articleTitle: Cone-Beam Reconstruction for Circular Scanning with Bilateral Truncation Based on the VFB Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We describe a new procedure, based on the virtual fan-beam (VFB) method, to perform volume-of-interest (VOI) reconstruction from cone-beam data acquired with a circular trajectory and bilateral transverse truncation of the projections. Our simulations with the Forbild thorax phantom suggest that this novel method gives, in a VOI, results quite similar to those obtained by the Feldkamp, Davis, Kress algorithm with non-truncated data.

articleTitle: A Survey of Machine Learning to FPGA Tool-Flows for Instrumentation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In the past decade, new developments in radiation and photonic detectors have caused significant improvements in resolution, sensitivity, readout rate and size, which all contribute to increased data generation rates. Analyzing this vast amount of data requires many processing units and communication cables between processing units and detectors. To overcome this problem, Edge Computing proposes to move computation units near the detectors. To handle non-linear mathematics relationships between data, Machine Learning (ML) is a powerful algorithm that has been widely used in different applications. Using ML near the edge is a new technique, called EdgeML. ML algorithms can be implemented in digital circuits such as ASICs and FPGAs to increase parallelization and pipelining. This paper discusses several current tool-flows that implement ML algorithms in FPGAs to achieve low latency and high throughput in an EdgeML system. We compare their ease-of-use, accessibility, and examine their performance for different purposes. We also implemented the most promising tool-flows to compare their actual performance on hardware, for instrumentation applications.

articleTitle: Integrated Preclinical PET-OT employing Monolithic Modules Comounted with Plenoptic Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Motivated by promising applications in the fields of pharmacokinetics, preclinical oncology research and tomographic optical imaging, the medical imaging community formerly took on the task of developing a multimodal detector system that would allow for simultaneous nuclear and optical imaging. These efforts began more than a decade ago but were not able to result in an applicable concept. This study reassesses the task and proposes a new approach to the challenge by presenting the blueprint for an integrated preclinical bi-modal system that fully merges PET imaging with optical tomography. Said blueprint is demonstrated through the investigation of a pilot system consisting of 10 detector modules (yielding an 83 mm inner-detector diameter), each combining a 25 x 25 x 25 mm monolithic scintillating LYSO crystal, read out by two 25 x 25 mm SiPM arrays coupled to perpendicular faces of the crystal, with a plenoptic detector mounted on the front face of the crystal. The feasibility of this detector concept was evaluated by studying both PET and optical imaging components through dedicated Monte Carlo simulation, followed by synergistic image reconstruction. Initial results are shown for two point sources, each 1 mm in diameter, separated centre-to-centre by 2 mm and placed at the centre of the field of view.

articleTitle: Electronics and 3He Counter Acquisition Tests During the Pulses of a D-T Neutron Generator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Nuclear logging industry uses Active Neutron Interrogation devices for geological prospection and exploitation. Modern neutron logging tools uses a pulsed neutron generator emitting fast neutrons (2.5 or 14.1 MeV) with an average emission in the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> range. Some measurement techniques rely on nonfully thermalized neutrons, called epithermal neutrons, which are less sensitive to neutron absorbers than thermal neutrons. The signal due to generator neutrons backscattered towards helium 3 proportional counter is used to assess hydrogen porosity. It decays within hundreds of microseconds. Historically, epithermal neutron measurements, with a cadmium layer around the detector, suffered of insufficient counting statistics. To parry this drawback, our goal is to perform the measurement during the neutron generator burst. Therefore, the detector and acquisition chain must be able to handle a high flux of neutrons. This work investigates the behavior of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>He counters with different gas additives, adapted either to charge or to current amplifiers, located close to a D-T neutron generator, with the same total detection efficiency we have in a logging tool. We tested instantaneous neutron emissions between 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> and 2.5∙10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> during generator pulses with a duration ranging from 40 to 800 µs. It appears that the throughput of the acquisition chain does not only depend on the generator instantaneous emission rate, but also on burst duration. Unexpectedly the maximum output count rate 4.4∙10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is thus reached with short generator pulses of 40 µs length and a very high instantaneous neutron emission 8.4∙10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, using a 30NH15CS <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>He counter adapted to G-ADSF10 current amplifier.

articleTitle: Texture-Enhanced Low Dose CT Image Denoising Using Pearson Divergence Loss
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Low-dose Computed Tomography (LDCT) image denoising using deep learning methods with mean-square error (MSE) loss is known to fall into regression-to-mean problem which results in over-smoothed edges and loss of textures in the image. To overcome this issue, we are interested in the utilization of stochastic function to improve the texture instead of using complicated networks or feature (latent) space losses. In this paper, we proposed a combined loss containing the MSE loss to learn mean distribution and the Pearson divergence loss to learn feature textures. Specifically, the Pearson divergence loss is computed in an image space rather than a feature space to measure the distance between two intensity measures of denoised LDCT image and the normal-dose CT (NDCT) image. In results, we exploit the conventional U-net and demonstrate that the proposed combined loss provides visually enhanced textures compared to the conventional MSE loss.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of a Triggerless Readout System for CDEX-100 HPGe Detector Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: The experiments based on germanium detectors which can explore low energy regions play an important role in the weekly interacting massive particles (WIMP) searching. CDEX-100 experiment aiming at the direct detection of light dark matter contains 100-kilogram HPGe detectors and will be held in CJPL-II underground laboratory. A preliminary design of a trigger-less readout system designed for CDEX-100 is introduced in this paper. The system can provide 128 sampling channels with 125 MSPS sampling rate and 16-Bit vertical resolution and use 2×PCIe 3.0×16 links which support 30GB/s transmission bandwidth for data uploaded. Commonly, in order to establish the energy threshold, the readout system will define the trigger level at a fixed number of baseline standard deviations (σ) above the baseline level, typical 5σ or more. However, this readout system can support triggerless readout of all sampling channels through ultra-high transmission bandwidth and on-line lossless data compression algorithms like Huffman coding. Then, it can provide lower energy threshold data for physical analysis to help the rare event searches.

articleTitle: Radiation-Tolerance Testing of FPGA-based, Self-reading Hadron Fluence Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Hadron fluence monitors based on static random access memories are being used at CERN and have been proposed for proton therapy facilities. Some of the limitations of the state of the art are related to the usage of separate components for sensing upsets and for reading them out, as these increase the power consumption, the board complexity and its size. Moreover, due to radiation-tolerance requirements, the readout logic is fixed and it cannot be updated once the system has been implemented. In this work, we describe an hadron fluence monitor using a static-random-access-memory-based field programmable gate array for implementing both the sensitive element and the readout logic. We irradiated two sensors prototypes at the Jožef Stefan Institute’s TRIGA Mark II research reactor, under different neutron flux conditions. We discuss our results, which include the measurements of the radiation tolerance in terms of 1-MeV neutron equivalent fluence and the average number of readable upsets before failure of the readout logic.

articleTitle: Pixelated Diamond Detector with High Density Waveform Readout for Charged Particle Beam Line Characterization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: In this report we describe a novel pixelated diamond detector for the measurement and characterization of accelerator beam particle bunches both spatially and temporally by utilizing on-detector trace lithography and read out by system-on-chip (SoC) high density waveform digitizers developed by Nalu Scientific LLC (NSL). The theory, detection methodology, and planned instrumentation will be discussed, as well as initial measurements.

articleTitle: Radon Transform Adaptation in Compton Reconstruction Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: While the diagnostic value of Compton Camera systems has become of major importance in clinical practice, the reconstruction of Compton data proves to be complicated. In order to localize a radioactive source, the Compton cone transform with respect to Compton kinematics is necessary. To this direction and despite the iterative and geometrical approaches already tested in Compton Imaging, an analytical reconstruction algorithm is proposed. For all recorded events, the Compton cone intersection with the different z planes results in solutions lying on ellipses while each pair of them is included in various y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">slices</inf>. Depending on the selected y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">slice</inf> and z plane, the generatrices of each cone form a V-line by connecting the vertex and the two points of the resulting ellipse. When identifying these V-lines as rays and their inclination from xy plane as projection angles, a sinogram-type matrix can be formed, on which the well-known inverse Radon Transform can be performed. The filtered inversion of the sinogram for each y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">slice</inf> reaches acceptable results and leads to 2D and 3D reconstruction of various distributions. A detailed description of this algorithmic scheme is presented along with preliminary reconstruction results of the method.

articleTitle: Neural Networks for Gamma Interaction Positioning in Continuous SPECT Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) detectors with improved spatial resolution are important to build SPECT systems with higher resolution or sensitivity. In this work we investigate whether the use of neural networks to position gamma interactions in SPECT detectors can lead to improved positioning performance. Networks are trained on calibration data of the SPECT detectors in the MOLECUBES γ-CUBE consisting of a continuous 50x46x5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> NaI(Tl) scintillator connected to an 8x8 SiPM photodetector array. Performance is compared with the currently used mean nearest neighbor positioning algorithm. Moreover, a data augmentation technique is proposed to prevent network overfitting to the training grid without the need to acquire additional validation data at intermediate positions. Superior positioning performance is obtained with the neural networks achieving a FWHM in the detector center of 0.90 mm versus 1.02 mm with mean nearest neighbor positioning. Floodmaps show a better uniformity with less hotspots at the SiPM pixel centers and the positioning event rate is significantly faster. These results show the potential of neural networks to further improve the performance of SPECT systems. Future work will investigate the effect on image quality and network interchangeability between detectors.

articleTitle: Analysis of Inter-Fraction Respiratory Variability Effect on Data-Driven Respiratory Signal Estimation Methods from CBCT Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Irregular breathing patterns appearing as apnea-like features in respiratory signals can occur within lung cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy treatments. Various data-driven methods used to extract respiratory signals from raw Cone-Beam CT (CBCT) projection data usually assumes that the signals are sinusoidal during free-breathing. The performance of these methods was previously studied comparatively on a set of clinical patient data. However, it did not encompass irregular breathing patterns. Thus, the purpose of this work is to further analyze the performance of the four data driven methods on five more sets of projection data on the same patient but displaying the involuntary breath-holding represented as apnea-like features during respiration. Other than the quantitative overall correlation coefficient values for each method and fraction against a reference signal, the local correlation is also evaluated and visually assessed for qualitative analysis. The results indicate that the Amsterdam Shroud (AS) method produced a higher inter-fraction mean overall local correlation coefficient value at 0.778 compared to the Local Principal Component Analysis (LPCA), Intensity Analysis (IA) and Fourier Transform-Phase (FTP) methods. Additionally, the qualitative plots showed that the FTP method also performed well in preserving the apnea-like features within its extracted signal. Thus, suggesting that the performance of current data driven methods can be distinctive with respect to the inter-fraction respiratory motion variations that occur during patient treatment.

articleTitle: Experimental Estimation of Gamma and Electron Detection Ratios for Training and Evaluating Signal Discriminators for Intraoperative Probes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Radioguided surgery (RGS) for cancer resection is a widely performed practice for accurate localisation of cancerous tissue. The medical radioisotope <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">99m</sup>Tc can be detected during RGS with the use of an intraoperative probe to detect cancerous tissue. For accurate localization, the internal conversion (IC) electrons from <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">99m</sup>Tc are set as the target emission due to their shorter range in tissue. However, the inability to isolate the IC electrons and gamma emissions mean that a labelled dataset is not available in practice, yet this is required for training a discriminator. In this study, an experimental method relying on evaporation is proposed to obtain ground truth information relating to emissions present within the dataset using physics-informed modelling of the IC electron and gamma signals. By experimental design, both signals vary differently over time thus allowing the ratio between the two signal sources to be estimated. This ground truth ratio information has been measured and hence used i) to assess the intrinsic response of an intraoperative probe for IC electron detection, and ii) to evaluate experimentally different discriminator algorithms. Furthermore, the data can also be used to partially label a measured dataset, allowing both training and testing of discriminators with known ratios. In summary, an experimental method was proposed to allow the evaluation of detector sensitivities and the development of discriminators for unlabelled datasets.

articleTitle: 2-D Nanoscale Coating for Optimized Light Extraction from Inorganic Scintillators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Gamma spectroscopy is used for various applications, including nuclear nonproliferation and safeguards, isotope identification, astronomy, and medical applications. Inorganic scintillators are widely used for gamma spectroscopy because of their energy resolution at room temperature, lower cost, and relatively high light yields. However, inorganic scintillators typically have a high refractive index, which results in substantial light losses due to total internal reflection. In this work, 2-D periodic nanostructure photonic crystals are used to provide an optical coupling between the scintillator and photosensor to mitigate the original light loss via constructive interference. Such photonic crystal geometry needs to be optimized for the specific scintillator material and photosensor. This optimization is performed using two simulation codes: Geant4 and OptiFDTD, to account for macroscale and nanoscale light transport, respectively. This coupled simulation tool has been used to find the optimized photonic crystal geometry for a LYSO scintillator coupled with Si3N4 photonic crystals. Preliminary simulation results with 2-D photonic crystals show more than 62% improvement in light transmission for the first pass of light through the photonic crystals. Reflections at the LYSO interfaces have not been simulated. Future work will incorporate reflections at all interfaces, more complex geometries, as well as optimized 3-D photonic crystals. The optimized 2-D geometries are being manufactured in the lab and characterized with various gamma sources to assess the resulting improvements in energy resolution.

articleTitle: Topology-based Cost Function: a Novel Approach for Organ Delineation in Medical Images with Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Medical images segmentation plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning. Manual segmentation is a tedious and time-consuming task for experts and prone to human errors; thus, many efforts have been made to automate this process and facilitate the hardships of manual segmentation. Among these methods, deep learning approaches showed tremendous progress in the accuracy of medical image segmentation and became a dominant method. Despite these achievements, deep learning methods suffer from a defect in comprehensively learning the shape/topology of the target object. This defect cause islands of voxels, topological inconsistency, and unrealistic shapes in the final segmentation. To address this defect, an initial guess as prior knowledge for deep neural networks was proposed, and others refine the final segmentation mask to eliminate islands of voxels and fill undesired holes. In spite of these efforts, the main problem of learning topological features in neural networks is still unsolved. In this study, we proposed a novel cost function that encourages the neural network to capture the underlying shape morphology of the segmentation target in 3D medical images. The key idea of our proposed method is to constitute a shape space by vectorizing the 3D segmentation masks and extracting eigenvectors of this space through exploiting Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method. With a weighted sum of extracted eigenvectors, reconstruction of the primary segmentation mask is available. Therefore, the reconstruction weights can discriminate between realistic and unrealistic shape topology in the final output. We realized that the kurtoses of reconstruction weights for realistic shapes are higher than those of unrealistic ones. Accordingly, by penalizing the network to generate higher kurtoses of reconstruction weights for predicted segmentation, more realistic/valid shapes are generated, and networks learn to extract topology-based features. We employed an MRI hippocampus segmentation dataset and a 3D fully convolutional segmentation network to validate this approach. The network is once trained with a conventional cost function (e.g., Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE)) and once with the topology-based cost function (ours). The quantitative evaluation for the test set showed an improvement from 0.81 to 0.86 in the Dice score. Furthermore, the defects such as islands of voxels and topological inconsistency vanished when the shape/morphology-based loss function was used.

articleTitle: Direct PET Parametric Imaging Using Deep Image Prior and a Parameter Amplification Strategy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: Direct parametric imaging in positron emission tomography (PET) is the technique of reconstructing pharmacokinetic parametric images directly from raw PET data. Nonlinear parametric imaging is challenging due to the high level of noise in the raw PET data and the complex mapping from kinetic parameters to the projection space. In this work, we proposed a parameter amplification strategy and incorporated deep image prior (DIP) and forward physical model to reconstruct parametric images of nonlinear compartmental model. We used a U-Net as generator to output multiple images from different channels, and each channel output was scaled by an amplification factor (AF) to obtain the parametric image. Amplification was applied on the parameters that had small values and less impact on the objective function modeled by Poisson measured data. The proposed DIP-AF method was tested on the two-tissue model using 30-minute dynamic <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F-FDG cardiac phantom data, and an AF of 10 was applied on k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Results showed that the DIP-based method outperformed than the traditional indirect method and an optimization transfer direct method (OTEM). The reconstructed k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> images using the proposed DIP-AF method showed less noise and better image structure compared to the DIP-only method, which demonstrated the effectiveness of the parameter amplification strategy

articleTitle: A Spectroscopic and Imaging Scintillator-Based Detector for Dose Monitoring in BNCT
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (NSS/MIC)
abstract: We report on the experimental characterization of a detection module based on a 2" cylindrical LaBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Ce+Sr) scintillator crystal, coupled to a matrix of 64 Silicon Photo-multipliers (SiPMs), developed as a basic element for a SPECT system for dose monitoring in Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT). The module is developed to detect the 478 keV gamma rays emitted by the excited <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>Li produced in the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>B(n, α)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>Li reaction, in order to have real-time monitoring of the dose released locally. Thanks to the good energy resolution of the detector (2.7% at 662 keV), the photopeak at 478 keV is well separated from the adjacent e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-annihilation photopeak at 511 keV, mainly originated from the pair production process due to the 2.2 MeV gamma rays created by the hydrogen-neutron capture. In this work, we present the results obtained by irradiating <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>B-loaded samples, with concentration as low as 62 ppm, with a neutron flux of approximately 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> n/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/s. Good linearity between the number of events detected at 478 keV and the boron concentration of the samples has been obtained. The first imaging results have been obtained with a 5cm×5cm×2cm square crystal and a Convolutional Neural Network for data elaboration.
